Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis targeting whole-brain task-based effects in healthy adults.

The study uses a Tower of London planning task that meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed planning/sequencing actions). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=17). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space with tables of peak activations, and the measured signal is BOLD. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not meet the review's problem-solving task definition (I5). The tasks involve navigating to or searching for personal files (file retrieval) and contrasts of navigation vs. search; while goal-directed, the paradigm is a memory/retrieval/navigation task rather than a defined problem-solving task requiring critical evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions to arrive at a novel or rule-based solution. All other inclusion criteria are satisfied: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), BOLD measure reported (I8), and coordinates reported in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, includes within-group task effects). Therefore exclude for failure to meet I5.

This fMRI study tests abstract reasoning/problem-solving (determine next picture in sequence), a task that fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed sequencing and rule-based solution). It reports whole-brain, group-level effects for healthy adult controls (one-sample t test, n=18), BOLD signal measures, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI with tables of peak activations. Results are voxelwise whole-brain analyses and reported in tables, which satisfies reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effect; empirical human data).

The task is goal-directed navigation (participants instructed to navigate to a target landmark), which includes planning/sequence of actions (self-localization, target localization, path planning) and thus fits the review definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports multiple group-level whole-brain analyses (several analyses state model fit and inference over whole brain; e.g., analyses 10–18), satisfying I6. Coordinate space is MNI and the paper reports peak coordinates in tables, satisfying I7 and I9. The measure is BOLD fMRI, satisfying I8. The document includes voxelwise peak tables and whole-brain corrected results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study investigates recognition/decision processes (episodic and lexical discrimination; same-different vs forced-choice), not goal-directed problem-solving as defined (no evidence of tasks requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to reach a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analysis present), I7 (MNI coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task as defined). No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E6 not met).

The task is a paced visual serial addition test requiring participants to apply an arithmetic rule (add each digit to the preceding digit) to achieve a goal — this fits the review's definition of problem-solving (rule-based algebraic operations). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) in healthy adults (n=9). Results include stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space with peak tables reported, and the measured outcome is BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise, corrected, whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only disease comparison, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusions are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of mental arithmetic that requires goal-directed operations (numerosity judgments and arithmetic operations), satisfying the review definition of problem solving (I5). It reports group-level, second-level random-effects analyses fit over the whole brain (many analyses list "Model fit over: whole brain" and PPI second-level results), satisfying I6. Results are reported in MNI stereotactic space with peak coordinates in tables, satisfying I7 and I9. The measured signal is BOLD (functional bold connectivity and activation), satisfying I8. Participants are healthy adults (n=27). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain voxelwise results (not ROI-only), reports within-group task effects in healthy adults, and is empirical. Therefore the article meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, voxelwise BOLD coordinates (MNI) and tables of peak coordinates; however the experimental paradigm is a spatial learning/virtual navigation task (inferring layout of a virtual town, drawing a map, indicating left/behind/right) focused on spatial memory and learning rather than on problem solving as defined by the review (goal-directed critical thinking processes such as evaluating, planning/sequencing actions within a rule-based framework to derive previously unknown solutions across domains). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Excluded because I5 is not met; all other relevant inclusion criteria that could be assessed are met.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest analyses (Model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to ROI), triggering exclusion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task involves goal-directed route planning/selection—problem solving), I7 (results reported in MNI coordinate space with peaks), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level analyses reported). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports task-based fMRI BOLD analyses of a logical problem-solving task (evaluating contradictory vs non-contradictory statements using Aristotelian logic), which requires goal-directed evaluation and application of logical rules (meets I5). It includes whole-brain, random-effects group-level analyses in healthy adults (n=13) with inference over the whole brain (meets I6). Results are reported in MNI space with peak coordinate tables (meets I7) and BOLD/fMRI measures are explicitly reported (meets I8). Coordinate results are provided in tables, satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not group-comparisons only, includes within-group healthy task effects, empirical data).

The study reports task-based fMRI BOLD results from a goal-directed virtual-navigation task requiring subjects to retrieve objects and remember/plan which arms to avoid—constituting problem-solving (goal, planning/sequencing, rule-based execution). It includes at least one whole-brain group-level analysis (Analysis 12843299_analysis_3: inference over whole brain, n=14), uses Talairach stereotactic space and reports peak coordinates/tables, and BOLD is the measured signal. Coordinate results are provided in tables and peaks. Although several analyses used ROI-restricted inference, the presence of a whole-brain group analysis prevents exclusion for ROI-only reporting. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study of mental arithmetic meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I5: The task (mental calculation across operators and complexities) fits the problem-solving definition—participants have a goal and apply rule-based operations to arrive at correct solutions. I6: Group-level whole-brain analyses are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; second-level random effects, n=11 healthy adults). I7: Coordinate space is reported as Talairach and peaks are provided in tables. I8: Measures include BOLD fMRI. I9: Voxelwise results are reported in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), the paper reports healthy within-group task effects (not only between-group or demographic comparisons), and it is empirical. Full text appears available through the NeuroStore record provided, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports an event-related, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults (n=18–23) requiring goal-directed navigation: participants encoded a goal on a map and had to plan and execute routes to reach it without landmarks, which fits the review's definition of problem solving (goal + need to figure out/plan and execute actions). The paper includes multiple whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t tests over whole brain) with reported stereotactic (MNI) peak coordinates in tables, and uses BOLD fMRI measures. Coordinates are reported in tables and thresholding/inference details are provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons).

The study investigates goal-directed route planning and related planning/execution processes during realistic virtual navigation—tasks that require establishing a goal and devising/sequencing actions to reach it, meeting the review's problem-solving definition (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; second-level t-tests) in healthy adults (n=20) meeting I6. Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with peak tables (I7,I9). The measured signal is BOLD (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not limited to between-group comparisons or patient groups, and the paper is empirical. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusions apply.

The task is an associative memory/labeling task (training nonmusicians to map chords to arbitrary labels) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing, or executing operations to derive novel solutions). While the study meets other methodological criteria (whole-brain group-level fMRI; stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI; BOLD measure; coordinate results available), it does not address problem-solving across domains. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of goal-directed navigation in healthy adults (n=17) with within-group contrasts comparing sequence-based and place-based strategies. The navigation task requires locating a goal and, in the sequence-based condition, planning/sequencing actions to reach it, meeting the review's definition of problem solving. Analyses were fit over the whole brain, report group-level task effects, and provide stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. The measure is BOLD fMRI. Coordinate peaks are reported in tables/analyses. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

The study reports a task-based fMRI BOLD experiment in healthy young adults (n=23) using a virtual radial-maze/wayfinding paradigm requiring goal-directed learning and flexible re-planning (fits the review's problem-solving definition). Group-level analyses were performed with model fit over the whole brain and reported stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) in tables. At least one analysis reports BOLD effects and coordinates, and results are available in tables. Although one analysis notes inference restricted to an ROI, the study nonetheless includes whole-brain model estimation and reports task-related coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The reported task is spatial navigation and landmark-based encoding/retrieval (virtual open-field navigation, remembering/replacing object locations). Although the study meets imaging and reporting requirements (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults, MNI coordinates, BOLD), it does not test a problem-solving paradigm as defined by the review (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions to arrive at a correct/novel solution within a rule-based framework). The task is memory/navigation-focused rather than requiring critical thinking or rule-based solution generation across domains. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met, while I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The task (unsolvable anagrams) qualifies as a problem-solving paradigm (I5). The study reports whole-brain group-level analyses (Analyses 24205247_analysis_0 and _2) in healthy adult males (I6), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7) with coordinates/tables available (I9). However, all reported voxelwise results in the document are between-group contrasts and group x condition interactions (HA vs LA and omnibus between-group effects); no within-healthy-group task > baseline activation maps or task-related increases in a healthy sample are reported. Therefore the study only reports between-group contrasts and lacks a healthy-group task effect, meeting exclusion criterion E5. Because E5 is met, the study must be excluded despite meeting I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses a task-based fMRI paradigm in healthy adults where participants solve difficult technical problems using heuristic prototypes (meets I5). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed with model fit and inference over the whole brain (I6). Results report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach and list reported peaks (I7, I9). The measured outcome is BOLD signal (I8). Participants are healthy adults (n=16). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons, and include within-group task effects in healthy participants. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study reports whole-brain BOLD results in MNI space (reported peaks) for a Hayling sentence completion task, so it meets I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD/fMRI outcome), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). However, the reported analyses are between-group contrasts (HC > HR who developed MDD; HR well > HR who developed MDD) and no within-group task-related activation map or healthy-group task effect is presented. Thus it appears to include only between-group contrasts and does not provide a healthy adult task effect as required. The task (Hayling sentence completion) is a language/response task and may not meet the review’s problem-solving definition (I5) either. Therefore the study is excluded under E5 (only between-group contrasts or no healthy-group task effect).

The study includes a healthy control group (n=10) with a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise BOLD analysis of the PASAT task reported in Talairach coordinates. The PASAT requires arithmetic sequencing and rule-based operations (summing last two digits), which meets the review's definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed operations following an algebraic rule). Coordinates and peaks are reported for the control group, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met.

The task is a goal-directed place-finding/navigation paradigm that requires locating targets, planning/sequencing a route, and executing actions—consistent with the review’s operational definition of problem solving (I5). The study used task-based fMRI with BOLD measure (I8), reported stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and includes group-level, second-level random-effects analyses with model fit over the whole brain (I6). Coordinate peaks are reported (I9). Although inference was performed with small-volume correction (ROI-restricted inference), the model was estimated over the whole brain and healthy adult participants were tested (n=22), so this does not meet exclusion E3 (reports only ROI results). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete in the provided record.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest analyses (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI including arithmetic tasks that involve rule-based operations consistent with problem-solving), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise peaks reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis reported; model fit and inference were restricted to predefined ROIs with small-volume correction). Therefore the study cannot be included in this whole-brain meta-analysis.

The task involves planning and executing pantomimed use of unfamiliar tools, which entails mechanical problem-solving processes (goal-directed planning/sequencing and inferring function from structure). The study is an empirical task-based fMRI BOLD study in healthy adults (n=16) reporting voxelwise whole-brain group-level analyses and peaks (Talairach coordinates) with tabulated results. These features satisfy the review’s requirements for a problem-solving task, whole-brain group effects, stereotactic coordinates, BOLD measure, and available voxelwise results in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting or non-empirical paper) are met.

This PET study uses the Tower of Toronto problem-solving task (goal-directed planning and ordered moves), meeting I5. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise PET analyses (model fit over whole brain; within-group contrasts) in healthy adults (n=12), meeting I6. Coordinate space is SPM99 MNI and peaks are reported in tables, meeting I7 and I9. The measure is cerebral blood flow (perfusion) via PET (rCBF), meeting I8. Voxelwise peak coordinates are provided in tables for contrasts of interest. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: results are whole-brain rather than ROI-only, not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons, include healthy-group task effects (within-group contrasts), and the paper is empirical. Therefore include.

This is a task-based fMRI study of numerical inductive/relational reasoning that requires participants to discover and apply rules (a goal-directed problem-solving task). It reports group-level whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) in healthy adult participants (n=16), uses BOLD contrast measures, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with reported peak tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes within-group task effects, empirical data). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in healthy adults (n=18) performing mental arithmetic (auditorily presented addition and subtraction), which fits the review’s problem-solving definition (rule-based operations to reach a correct solution) satisfying I5. Analyses were whole-brain group-level (RFX) voxelwise GLM results reported as peak coordinates in MNI space and BOLD signal, meeting I6, I7, and I8. Coordinate tables are reported (reported peaks/tables), satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not only disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), include within-group healthy task effects (so E5 not met), and the paper is empirical (E6 not met). Full text is available in the NeuroStore record provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Overall, all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered, so INCLUDE.

The study uses the Tower of London task (a problem-solving/planning task) and reports BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates; however, the reported analysis was fit and inference restricted to a region-of-interest (ROI) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise group analysis. This violates the requirement for at least one whole-brain group-level analysis (I6) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This task-based fMRI study uses the Raven’s Progressive Matrices (a canonical problem-solving/fluid-reasoning task) and reports whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults (within-group contrast for the non-autistic healthy sample, n=18). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (reported peaks/tables). The imaging measure is BOLD signal. Voxelwise whole-brain analyses and PPI connectivity analyses are reported with coordinate tables. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for a problem-solving task, whole-brain healthy adult group effects, standardized coordinates, and BOLD-based analyses.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of deductive reasoning and mathematical problem solving (meets I5). Model was fit over the whole brain and inference was whole-brain at the group level with n=16 participants (meets I6). Coordinates are reported in Talairach and peaks are listed in a table (meets I7 and I9). Measure is BOLD (meets I8). No exclusion criteria apply: results are whole-brain voxelwise (not ROI-only), participants are a single healthy group (no between-group-only contrasts or patient comparisons), and the paper is empirical. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using RPM-adapted matrices that requires goal-directed problem solving and relational integration (meets I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level within-subject contrasts in healthy adults (n=8), satisfying I6. Results report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space with peak tables (I7,I9). Measure is BOLD functional response (I8). Thresholding and reported peak tables indicate voxelwise, whole-brain task-related increases. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and include healthy-group task effects. The extracted document appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This PET study measured regional cerebral blood flow during a mental arithmetic (serial subtraction) task and reports whole-brain, group-level task>rest activation for healthy control participants (Analysis 15110005_analysis_4). Mental arithmetic (serial subtraction) meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed, rule-based operations). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space with peak coordinates in tables, and rCBF (perfusion) analyses are explicitly reported. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach), I8 (rCBF analysis), and I9 (coordinates reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain analyses are reported, a healthy-group task effect is present).

This fMRI study used a syllogistic deductive reasoning task (goal-directed, rule-based logical problem solving) with event-related design and within-subject contrasts, meeting the review definition of problem solving (I5). Analyses were whole-brain random-effects group-level BOLD analyses (Model fit over: whole brain; random effects t-tests), satisfying I6 and I8. Reported stereotactic peaks are in MNI space (Coordinate space: MNI), satisfying I7; voxelwise results (reported peaks) are present in the extracted analyses, satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient-group comparisons, includes healthy adult task effects, empirical).

Excluded because the task is a visual imagery/perceptual comparison task, not a problem-solving task per the review's I5 definition. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level PET analysis reported), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach), I8 (rCBF/PET measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is mental imagery/comparison, not a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to find novel solutions). No exclusion criteria were triggered (no ROI-only results, no between-group-only contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text is complete as provided.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment using the Remote Associates Task, which meets the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed word-combination to reach a correct solution). It includes group-level, whole-brain analyses (second-stage random-effects GLM; model fit over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=13, ages 18–29). Results are reported in stereotactic Talairach space with reported peak coordinates and the neuroimaging measure is BOLD. Voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (insight > noninsight; problem onset) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group healthy task effects).

The study reports an fMRI task in healthy adults (n=16) requiring goal-directed route retrieval and adaptation (e.g., detour conditions) that involves identifying/planning a path to reach a goal—consistent with the review's operational definition of problem solving. It uses whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses and reports voxelwise stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables of peak coordinates). The neuroimaging measure is BOLD. Voxelwise results are reported in tables and figures per NeuroStore. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (goal-directed route-finding/planning), I6 (whole-brain group RFX), I7 (MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD measure) and I9 (voxelwise results in tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is available via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports an event-related mental arithmetic task (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) requiring goal-directed computation and rule-based operations, meeting the review's definition of problem solving (I5). It includes a whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis (model fit over: whole brain; n=11 healthy adults), satisfying I6. Peaks are reported in Talairach space with 58 coordinates (I7) and the measured signal is BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise results are reported in tables (reported peaks), which meets I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs (E3), are not only group comparisons by disease/age/gender (E4), include within-group task effects in healthy participants (so E5 does not apply), and this is empirical data (E6 not applicable). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports a task that meets the review's problem-solving definition (mental arithmetic: serial addition with a goal and rule-based operations), includes a group-level whole-brain second-level analysis in healthy adults (n=16), reports BOLD measures, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (peaks in table). Thresholding and model details indicate voxelwise whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The task is an explicit categorization requiring subjects to discover and apply changing abstract rules (rule learning), which fits the review’s definition of problem-solving. The study reports a whole-brain, voxelwise analysis (model fit over: whole brain) with group-level effects in healthy adults (n=8), uses BOLD fMRI, and reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach with peak coordinates (Table 1). Voxelwise results are presented (reported peaks) and inference is whole-brain. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical). Thus all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study of numerical inductive reasoning (rule induction and rule induction+application), which fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed rule-based identification and application). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (one-sample t-tests on individual contrast images) in healthy adult participants (n=20). Results are reported in MNI space with stereotactic peaks/tables, and the measured outcome is BOLD response. Coordinate tables and voxelwise thresholds are provided. No exclusion criteria apply: findings are not ROI-only, not restricted to disease/age/gender comparisons, and include within-group task effects in healthy adults. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are met and no exclusions are triggered.

The PASAT is an arithmetic/working-memory task that requires goal-directed sequencing and rule-based operations to arrive at correct sums, meeting the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports a whole-brain, group-level one-sample analysis of healthy adults (n=18) for PASAT>REPEAT (Model fit over: whole brain; random-effects), satisfying I6. Results are reported in Talairach space with peak coordinates in tables, satisfying I7 and I9. The imaging measure is BOLD fMRI, satisfying I8. Voxelwise whole-brain results are provided (not ROI-only), and a within-group healthy control task effect is present, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears available from the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The virtual navigation task meets the review’s definition of problem-solving (goal-directed search, planning/sequencing actions to find target stores). Participants are healthy adults (n=15). The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses (e.g. Analysis 22786703_analysis_3: whole-brain inference; multiple connectivity analyses fit and inferred over whole brain) and reports stereotactic results in MNI space with reported peaks/tables. BOLD measures are reported. Results are available in tables/figures per the record. Although some ROI analyses are present, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported, so the study is not limited to ROIs. No exclusion criteria apply. Thus all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

The study investigates route learning/navigation (route vs survey perspectives) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed need to figure out a way to reach a solution involving critical thinking, planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a correct/novel solution). Tasks reported are learning/encoding routes and maps, not explicit problem solving. The paper does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level BOLD fMRI analyses (I6, I8), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI (I7), and provides voxelwise results in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore excluded because it does not satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) The task requires problem solving (participants determine the next best chess move — goal-directed evaluation, planning, and rule-based execution). (I6) A whole-brain analysis is reported (model fit over: whole brain) on healthy adult participants (n=6, ages 24–33). (I7) Task-related increases are reported as stereotactic coordinates (Talairach; 18 peaks in table). (I8) The measured signal is BOLD (functional bold response). (I9) Voxelwise results are reported in tabulated coordinates. Although the analysis is described as fixed-effects, the record nevertheless reports group-level whole-brain task effects in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) The task is mental arithmetic (single-digit addition, subtraction, multiplication), which involves goal-directed, rule-based problem solving (algebraic/arithmetic operations); (I6) Whole-brain, group-level analyses are reported for a healthy adult sample (n=8, mean age 44.1) with within-group contrasts; (I7) Coordinates are reported in Talairach space; (I8) The measured signal is BOLD fMRI; (I9) Voxelwise results are reported as peak coordinates in tables. No exclusion criteria apply: results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), the paper reports healthy adult task effects (not only between-group comparisons or clinical/age/gender-only effects), and it is empirical human data. The NeuroStore extract provides sufficient detail (tasks, whole-brain inference, coordinates, BOLD measure) to include the adult task contrasts in the meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults performing an inductive reasoning/rule-discovery task that requires setting a goal and inferring rules to predict outcomes, which fits the review's problem-solving definition (I5). Analyses were performed and reported at the whole-brain level with group effects (n=20 healthy adults) and inference over the whole brain (I6). Results are given in MNI stereotactic space (I7) and the measured signal is BOLD fMRI (I8). NeuroStore lists reported peaks/coordinates (acceptable per I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, are within-group task effects in healthy adults, and this is empirical data. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusions apply.

This fMRI study tests visuo-spatial and analogical reasoning tasks that require integrating relations to judge progressions (a goal-directed problem-solving/relational reasoning task). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (3-Relation > 1-Relation) with FDR-corrected results and tables of peak coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI (n=20 healthy adults). Although one contrast reports ROI-restricted inference, the study also provides whole-brain corrected results, so it is not ROI-only. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because inclusion criterion I7 is not met: the NeuroStore record specifies 'Coordinate space: OTHER', indicating that stereotactic coordinates are not reported in Talairach or MNI standardized space. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of problem solving using compound remote-associate problems), I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis, n=25), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (voxelwise peaks reported in Table 1). No exclusion criteria apply (none of E3–E6 are met).

The study reports an fMRI task requiring subjects to discover rules (goal-directed pattern discovery; evaluate sequences, form hypotheses, and predict targets), which meets the review’s problem-solving definition (I5). Analyses were modeled over the whole brain with group-level effects in 20 healthy adults (I6). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with tabulated peaks (I7, I9). The measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). Thresholding and reported contrasts indicate within-group task effects (not only between-group) and whole-brain inference; no ROI-only reporting or non-empirical design. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears accessible via the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest–restricted inference for all reported analyses (Inference restricted to: region of interest), which meets exclusion criterion E3. Although the model was fit over the whole brain, all significance testing is ROI-restricted and only ROI-corrected peaks are reported, so this effectively reports only ROI results. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (anagram solving is a problem-solving task), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD measure), I9 (coordinates/tables available). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (does not provide at least one whole-brain group-level analysis reported at the whole-brain inference level). Therefore EXCLUDED (exclusion E3).

The simulated orbital docking task is goal-directed and requires planning/sequencing and execution of actions to reach a docking goal, meeting the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with group-level within-subject contrasts in healthy adults (n=6; crossover design), satisfying I6. Results are reported in Talairach space (I7) and the measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). Coordinate results are presented in a table of peaks (Table 1), satisfying I9. Although contrasts are comparisons between sleep conditions (SD vs NS) rather than a simple task>baseline contrast, the reported activations are task-related effects during the problem-solving navigation task and therefore relevant. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Note: small sample size and liberal thresholding are methodological limitations but do not violate inclusion criteria.

All inclusion criteria are met. The study is a task-based fMRI investigation contrasting an ill-structured design task with a well-structured problem-solving task (I5). It reports group-level whole-brain analyses with inference reported over the whole brain (Analyses 3 and 4), satisfying I6. Coordinates are given in MNI space and peaks are reported in tables (I7, I9). BOLD signal is the measured outcome (I8). Participants are healthy adults (n=17). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain voxelwise results (not ROI-only), presents within-subject healthy-group task effects, and is empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a mental arithmetic verification task (subjects compute and evaluate correct vs incorrect equations), which constitutes problem solving within an algebraic rule set. The analysis is whole-brain, group-level (random-effects; n=16, ages 16–23), reports BOLD responses, and provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach (reported peaks in a table). All required inclusion criteria (I5–I9) are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of elementary deductive reasoning, which constitutes a logical problem-solving task (meets I5). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (model fit over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=14) (I6). Results are reported in stereotactic space (MNI) with peak coordinates/tables (I7, I9). The neuroimaging measure is BOLD (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), they report within-group task effects in healthy participants, and this is empirical primary data. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of metaphor comprehension/analogical mapping (reading 3-sentence passages) in healthy adults (n=24). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, BOLD results in MNI space, and voxelwise peak coordinates (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the task is language comprehension/metaphor interpretation, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no explicit goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing actions, or rule-based solution operations are described). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore EXCLUDED: inclusion criteria met = I6, I7, I8, I9; inclusion criterion not met = I5; exclusion criteria met = none (E: []).

Study uses FDG-PET in 12 regular marijuana users with primary cannabis dependence (not healthy adults). Although the task (virtual maze) fits the review's problem-solving definition (I5) and whole-brain MNI coordinates are reported (I7) and voxelwise results appear available (I9), the sample is not healthy and no healthy-group task effects are reported (violating I6). Additionally, the imaging measure is metabolic rate (FDG glucose uptake), not BOLD or rCBF (violating I8). Thus exclusion applies (E5: no healthy-group task effect).

The study reports a mental-arithmetic task that requires goal-directed operations and rule-based computations (adding consecutive numbers to reach a sum), meeting the review definition of problem solving (I5). It includes whole-brain group-level within-subject effects in healthy adults (n=12; whole-brain model fit and within-group contrasts), satisfying I6. Results are reported in stereotactic space (Talairach) with reported peak coordinates, satisfying I7. The measure is BOLD (functional bold), satisfying I8. Voxelwise peak results are available in the NeuroStore record, acceptable per I9. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain not ROI-only (not E3), not limited to only disease/age/gender comparisons (not E4), include healthy-group task effects (not E5), and the paper is empirical (not E6). Full text appears sufficiently represented in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment using deductive (syllogistic) problem-solving, which meets the review definition of problem solving (I5). It includes whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses in healthy adults (n=26) with several contrasts tested over the whole brain (I6). Results are reported in MNI space (coordinate space: MNI) and peaks/tables are provided (I7, I9). The measure is BOLD functional response (I8). Although one analysis used an ROI-restricted inference, multiple whole-brain FWE-corrected voxelwise results are reported, so E3 (ROI-only) does not apply, and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults (n=13) involving arithmetic problem solving (trained and untrained multiplication problems), which meets the review’s definition of problem solving as application of rule-based operations to reach correct solutions. Whole-brain, group-level second-level one-sample t-tests are reported. Results are given as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (tables of peaks), and the measure is BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are reported in tables. Therefore it satisfies I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only group comparisons, not non-empirical).

This fMRI study examines mental calculation (sequential multiplication/division, rule-based arithmetic), a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed operations and rule-based execution, meeting the review's problem-solving definition (I5). Analyses were whole-brain (model fit over whole brain) with group-level within-group contrasts reported (fixed-effects group analysis), satisfying I6. Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with peaks listed in Table 1, meeting I7 and I9. The neuroimaging measure is BOLD response (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to group comparisons of disease/age/gender (E4), include healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E5), and the paper is empirical (E6). Note: sample size is small (n≈5) and a fixed-effects model limits generalizability, but these do not violate inclusion criteria. Full text appears available via the extracted NeuroStore record.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (subtraction and multiplication) in healthy adults (n=10) using BOLD contrast. The study performed whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables of peaks). Mental arithmetic meets the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed, rule-based operations). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical group comparisons, includes within-group task effects, and is empirical).

The task is goal-directed maze navigation requiring subjects to select actions and update beliefs to reach a specified goal, which fits the review’s problem-solving definition (I5). The study reports whole-brain voxelwise model fit and inference at the group level in healthy adults (n=13, ages 23–28) (I6). Coordinates are given in MNI space with reported peaks (I7, I9). The measured outcome is BOLD (functional MRI) (I8). Thresholding and reported peaks indicate voxelwise task-related increases. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group or clinical comparison only, and not non-empirical).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it examines an inductive reasoning/number-series problem-solving task (goal-directed rule inference and execution), reports whole-brain random-effects group analyses (model fit over whole brain, one-sample t-tests, n=15 healthy adults), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with peak tables, and uses BOLD fMRI measures. NeuroStore extraction shows voxelwise coordinate results (tables of peaks) satisfying acceptable reporting. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs, are within healthy-group task effects (within-group contrasts present), and it is an empirical human neuroimaging study. Therefore include.

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive/relational reasoning (logical problem solving), using BOLD measures in healthy adult participants (n=16). Analyses were fit over the whole brain with group-level voxelwise contrasts and a parametric modulation, and reported stereotactic peak coordinates in MNI space (peaks listed in tables). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis), I7 (MNI coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (voxelwise results available in tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study reports whole-brain, group-level rCBF results in Talairach space for mental rotation tasks, but the experimental task (mental rotation / same vs mirror judgments of objects/hands) is a perceptual-spatial transformation task rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (which requires goal-directed problem identification/planning/sequencing or execution of operations within a rule set to reach a solution). The record contains within-group and between-group contrasts, whole-brain analyses, and stereotactic coordinates, satisfying I6, I7, I8 and I9, but provides no evidence that the task involves the problem solving processes required by I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This study is excluded because it reports only between-group contrasts (higher competence > lower competence) without clear within-group task-related activations; thus it meets exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of a mathematical/representation-matching task involving evaluation and arithmetic operations consistent with problem-solving), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD measure reported), and I9 (peaks reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all relevant inclusion criteria satisfied). The NeuroStore record shows only between-group, whole-brain contrasts and group comparisons of competence; no task>baseline or within-group task effects are provided in the document, triggering E5. fulltext_incomplete set to false.

This study examines arithmetic (exact/approximate calculation), which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). It reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and provides voxelwise peak tables (I9). However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group (children vs. adults) contrasts and ROI-restricted interaction results; no whole-brain, within-healthy-adults group-level task activation is reported. Therefore it fails I6 and meets exclusion criteria E5 (reports only between-group contrasts / lacks a healthy-group task effect). It also effectively only reports age-related group comparisons (children vs adults), invoking E4. Based on these, the study is excluded.

The study is an event-related task-based fMRI study of three-term relational (deductive) reasoning in healthy adults (n=14). The task requires evaluating whether a conclusion follows logically from premises, which meets the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed logical evaluation). The report includes whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with inference over the whole brain, voxel-level RFT correction, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI (peaks reported in Table tbl2). The measure is BOLD. Coordinate results are tabulated. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses arithmetic tasks that meet the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). It reports whole-brain voxelwise BOLD results with stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates in tables (I7, I8, I9). However, the NeuroStore record shows within-group whole-brain task effects only for children; there are no reported within-group whole-brain task effects for healthy adult participants (only between-group contrasts adults > children and children > adults). Therefore it does not satisfy I6 (a whole-brain group-level adult task effect). Because the paper lacks any adult within-group task effect, it falls under exclusion E5 (includes only between-group contrasts or does not include any healthy-group task effect). Conclusion: EXCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI of fluid reasoning tasks (Visualization and Induction) in healthy adults (n=22, age 20–24). The tasks require selecting the correct figure from alternatives (goal-directed reasoning/inductive and visuospatial problem-solving), which meets the review’s problem-solving task definition. Analyses were whole-brain (model fit and inference over whole brain) with group-level, random-effects, within-group contrasts (Visualization>Induction; Induction>Visualization). Results include stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space and report BOLD-based functional connectivity measures. Coordinate results are tabulated (reported peaks). The study is not ROI-only (seed-based connectivity but whole-brain inference). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses effortful mental arithmetic (initial subtraction/counting tasks) that meets the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations within a rule set). It reports whole-brain, group-level PET analyses in healthy adults (n=6) with model fit and inference over the whole brain. Results are presented as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (tables of reported peaks). The imaging measure is regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF). These satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy-task effects). Small sample size noted but does not violate inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of logical/transitive reasoning (abstract syllogisms), which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (operations conforming to a logical rule set to reach inferred solutions). The study reports group-level, whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) in healthy adult participants (n=17). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (tables of peaks) and the measured outcome is BOLD signal. Thresholding and corrected inference are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses PET with (18)FDG to measure regional cerebral metabolic rate for glucose (CMRglu) during a mental arithmetic task (meets I5: task is problem-solving; I6: whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults; I9: coordinates reported in a table). However it does not meet I8 because it does not report BOLD or rCBF measures (it reports CMRglu from FDG-PET). It also fails I7: although stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates are reported, they report only baseline > 24 h sleep deprivation decreases (no task-related increases were reported; authors note no significant increases), so it does not provide the required task-related activation increases in stereotactic space. No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are met. Therefore exclude due to unmet inclusion criteria I7 and I8.

The study reports an fMRI investigation of a logical deduction (problem-solving) task where subjects infer a hidden 4-key sequence—meeting the problem-solving definition (goal-driven inference, planning/sequencing, rule-based logical deduction). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=16, mean age 23). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and BOLD was the measured signal. Multiple within-group contrasts and parametric BOLD associations are reported with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates in tables. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs, are not only disease/age/gender comparisons, and are empirical. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are satisfied.

This PET study does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The verbal fluency (generate words beginning with a letter) is a language/executive retrieval task and does not clearly involve the critical-thinking, planning/sequencing, or rule-based problem-solving operations as specified by I5. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults are reported), I7 (results reported in Talairach coordinates), I8 (regional cerebral blood flow analysis via PET), I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because I5 is not met.

Excluded. Primary reason: the study does not include healthy adult participants—samples are adolescents (mean ages ~14–15), so inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adult individuals) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results reported in MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results/peak coordinates reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no healthy adult group), I5 (the Embedded Figures Task is described as an executive/reasoning/perceptual task but the document does not clearly establish it meets the review's definition of a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (analyses reported are mainly between-group contrasts/interactions and no clear within-group healthy-adult task effect is presented). Full text is available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study directly examines arithmetic calculation (addition of four numbers), which fits the review's definition of problem solving (a goal-directed task requiring rule-based operations to reach a correct solution) (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adults (n=14) with inference over the whole brain (I6). Results are given as stereotactic peaks in MNI space (coordinate space: MNI) and peak tables are reported (I7, I9). The imaging measure is BOLD response (I8). Thresholding and cluster/voxel-level corrections are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), effects are within healthy-group task contrasts (not only between-group or disease/age/gender comparisons), and this is empirical human data. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an event-related, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults performing syllogistic logical reasoning (deductive task), which fits the review's problem-solving definition (I5). Analyses were whole-brain with group-level within-subject contrasts and reported peak coordinates in MNI space (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain; coordinate space: MNI), satisfying I6 and I7. The reported measure is BOLD (functional bold), satisfying I8. Voxelwise results/peaks are reported (Reported peaks: 2 per contrast), satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons, include healthy-group task effects, and are empirical. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are satisfied and no exclusions apply.

The study investigates a virtual reality spatial memory/navigation task (encoding and reproduction of routes) in concussed athletes and controls. While the task has a goal (reproduce a route), the paper frames it as spatial memory/navigation rather than an explicit problem-solving paradigm involving evaluation, planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel solution or rule-based operations as required by I5. Therefore it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). It does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level task effects in healthy adults are reported (I6), results are given in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) (I7), BOLD fMRI measures are reported (I8), and coordinate results are present in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Consequently I exclude the paper because it fails inclusion criterion I5.

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) in healthy adults performing arithmetic tasks (digit naming, comparison, multiplication, subtraction). These tasks involve executing rule-based operations to arrive at correct solutions and thus meet the review's operational definition of problem solving (I5). The analysis is a whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis (model fit over whole brain; group analysis; n=8 healthy adults), satisfying I6. Results are reported in standardized stereotactic space (Talairach) as coordinate tables, meeting I7 and I9. The measure is BOLD, meeting I8. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), include within-group task effects in healthy participants (not E5), and the paper is empirical (not E6). Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

The study reports task-based BOLD fMRI of a canonical problem-solving/planning task (Tower of London) that fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed planning/sequencing). It includes whole-brain, group-level analyses for healthy adult controls (within-group planning>rest), uses Talairach coordinate space, and reports stereotactic peak coordinates in tables. BOLD measure is explicitly stated. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study investigates mental arithmetic (two-digit addition/subtraction), reports whole-brain voxelwise BOLD results in MNI space, and includes healthy participants in between-group analyses, so it meets I5 (problem-solving task), I7 (stereotactic coordinates, MNI), I8 (BOLD), and I9. However, the NeuroStore record shows only (a) within-patient whole-brain contrasts and (b) between-group patient>healthy interaction contrasts; it does not report a healthy-group, within-group task effect (i.e. a whole-brain group-level task effect for healthy adults). Thus the study does not satisfy I6 and appears to present only between-group contrasts or lacks a healthy-group task effect, meeting exclusion E5. Therefore it must be excluded.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) results and presents only between-group contrasts without a healthy-group task effect. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (ROI-only results) and E5 (only between-group contrast/no healthy-group task effect). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task is mental arithmetic, a problem-solving task), I7 (results reported in Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD measure reported), I9 (reported peaks in a table). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults; model fit is ROI and thresholding is region-level). Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

The study uses a perceptual maze task that meets the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed maze navigation requiring planning/sequencing). It reports rCBF PET results and gives stereotactic coordinates (Talairach). However, the NeuroStore extraction indicates model fitting and inference were performed over a predefined region-of-interest matrix (Model fit over: region of interest; Regions: predefined matrix), i.e. ROI-only analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise group analyses. This violates inclusion criterion I6 (requires at least one whole-brain group-level analysis) and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Accordingly the study is excluded.

The study investigates mental rotation (hand and viewer perspective transformations), which is a visuospatial transformation/perception task rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no evidence of planning, sequencing actions, or executing operations to reach a novel solution within a rule-based problem-solving framework). All other inclusion criteria are satisfied: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random effects analyses in healthy adults, n=18), I7 (coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure), I9 (reported voxelwise peaks/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (E3–E6 do not apply). Therefore excluded for failing I5 (not a problem-solving task).

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment using a deductive/relational reasoning task that requires evaluating whether conclusions follow from premises (a rule-based logical problem-solving process), satisfying the problem-solving definition. It includes whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference at the group level in healthy adults (n reported), reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach and peak tables, and uses BOLD as the measured signal. Voxelwise results are reported in tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply based on the provided document.

The task (virtual wayfinding: find grocery store from school) meets the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports BOLD fMRI measures (I8) and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with coordinate tables (I7, I9). However, it does NOT provide a whole-brain group-level analysis reporting task-related effects for healthy adults: the healthy within-group analysis is inference-restricted to a region-of-interest, and whole-brain results are only reported for between-group contrasts (controls>patients). Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (at least one whole-brain analysis with group-level effects in healthy adult individuals) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the document.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of arithmetic strategy selection, which fits the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed estimation requiring strategy evaluation, planning, and rule-based operations). It reports whole-brain random-effects group analyses in healthy adults (n=18, ages 19–30), uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach with reported peak tables (Table t3). Voxelwise results are reported and thresholding/inference is whole-brain. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an event-related task of mental arithmetic (two-digit × one-digit multiplication) that requires rule-based problem solving (algebraic operations, goal-directed calculation and selection of the closest solution), satisfying the review's definition of problem solving. It is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=18) with whole-brain, random-effects group analyses using BOLD. Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables of peaks), and voxelwise whole-brain inference is described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, not a review). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This is a task-based PET study using the Tower of London planning task, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning and sequencing of moves). The study reports whole-brain group-level within-subject contrasts (model fit over whole brain) in healthy adult participants (n=10 males). Results include reported stereotactic peaks in MNI space (tables with reported peaks) and the measured signal is cerebral blood flow (rCBF). Voxelwise results are reported in tables/peaks. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not limited to patient/group comparisons; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical data). Full text is available via the NeuroStore record substitute, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study includes a mental-arithmetic task that meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed, algebraic operations to arrive at a correct result). Imaging methods and results meet the meta-analysis requirements: whole-brain GLM analyses with group-level effects in healthy adult participants, BOLD as the measured signal, and stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space (peaks/tables provided). Voxelwise results are reported (tables of peaks) and inference was performed over the whole brain. The paper does not report only ROI results nor is it non-empirical. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This task-based fMRI study used a Raven's Progressive Matrices reasoning paradigm (a canonical problem-solving task requiring goal-directed rule discovery and application), reported group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, provided stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space, and reported BOLD activation peaks. Voxelwise, whole-brain inference was performed and coordinate peaks are reported in tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy within-group task effects). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. The task is a mental arithmetic problem-solving task (evaluating presented multiplication solutions and applying multiplication rules), satisfying I5. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level RFX-GLM results in healthy adult participants (n=10), satisfying I6. Results are reported in Talairach coordinates (I7) and the measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). Coordinate results and peaks are reported in tables as extracted (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons, and include within-subject task effects in healthy adults. Full text is available via the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=42) that used a mental-arithmetic problem-solving task requiring participants to compute answers (goal-directed operations following algebraic/arithmetical rules). Whole-brain group-level analyses were performed (model fit and inference over whole brain; one-sample t-tests), coordinates reported in MNI space with tables of peaks, and the measure is BOLD. These features satisfy the review objectives and all inclusion criteria: task-based problem solving (I5), whole-brain group effects in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinates in MNI (I7), BOLD analysis (I8), and reported coordinates/tables acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy task effects).

This study reports only ROI-based fMRI analyses: model fit and inference were restricted to an anatomical medial temporal lobe ROI (no whole-brain model/inference). Therefore it violates inclusion criterion I6 (requires at least one whole-brain, group-level analysis) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task is goal-directed navigation with a need to find a way to a target landmark), I7 (results reported in MNI space coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). However, because no whole-brain analyses are reported, the study must be excluded. Full text is available in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study investigates syllogistic deductive/relational reasoning (256 syllogistic arguments; subjects judge truth of conclusions) — a logical problem-solving task involving goal-directed evaluation and rule-based operations, meeting I5. Participants are healthy adults (n=20). Multiple analyses report whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference with group-level random-effects results (FWE-corrected), satisfying I6. Coordinate space is MNI and reported peaks are provided, satisfying I7. The measure is BOLD fMRI, satisfying I8. Task-related voxelwise results are reported (analyses/tables/peaks), so I9 is satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (ROI-only results are present but not exclusive; whole-brain effects reported).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI investigation of mental arithmetic that fits the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed computation using rule-based operations and execution) (I5). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, random-effects (n=16 healthy adults) satisfying I6. Results are reported in stereotactic space (MNI305) with coordinate tables (I7) and the measured signal is BOLD (functional bold) (I8). Coordinate results are presented in tables, acceptable per I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not solely group comparisons, and the study is empirical. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults (n=16) using a sequencing/route judgment task (determine correct sequential order), which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (planning/sequencing actions to reach a goal). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain for multiple contrasts), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (reported peaks/tables), and uses BOLD as the measured signal. Voxelwise results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes within-group healthy task effects). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment of deductive (syllogistic) reasoning in healthy adults (n=14), which fits the review's problem-solving definition (logical reasoning to determine whether conclusions follow). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain) with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and reports significant peak coordinates; the measure is BOLD. Multiple contrasts and corrected voxelwise thresholds are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, are within healthy-group task effects, and the study is empirical. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (training/transfer of multiplication to division) that clearly meets the review objective of problem-solving across domains. It satisfies I5: the mental arithmetic task requires goal-directed problem-solving (apply arithmetic rules to reach correct solutions). It satisfies I6: multiple whole-brain, group-level (second-level) analyses are reported in healthy adult participants (n=17). It satisfies I7: results are reported in MNI stereotactic space with reported peaks/tables. It satisfies I8: the measure is BOLD (functional bold response). It satisfies I9: voxelwise results/peaks are reported in tables (reported peaks and tbl4). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only between-group comparisons, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be included.

This PET study investigates abacus-based mental calculation (a goal-directed arithmetic task requiring rule-based operations and sequencing), meeting the review's definition of problem solving. It reports multiple whole-brain, group-level task contrasts in healthy adult participants (within-group and between-group analyses). Results are given as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with reported peak coordinates in tables, and the measured signal is cerebral blood flow (rCBF) from PET. Coordinate tables are explicitly noted. No exclusion criteria are met: findings are not restricted to ROIs, the study includes healthy-group task effects (not only between-group comparisons), and it is empirical human neuroimaging. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

The task is a spatial navigation/memory retrieval task (recognizing which maze a landmark belonged to from static images) and does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (no goal-directed planning, sequencing, or execution of operations to derive a solution during the scanned task). Other inclusion criteria are satisfied: whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults (n=18) (I6), results reported in MNI coordinates (I7), BOLD measure reported (I8), and voxelwise results reported (I9). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I5 (problem-solving task).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults performing arithmetic verification and magnitude-judgment tasks that involve rule-based operations (retrieval/checking of multiplication answers and numerical comparisons), meeting the review definition of problem solving (I5). The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain model fitting and inference and reports group-level activation peaks collapsed over subjects (table tbl3), satisfying I6. Coordinates are provided in Talairach space (I7). The measured signal is BOLD (I8). Voxelwise results are reported as coordinate tables/peaks (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, healthy-group task effects are reported, and the study is empirical. Full text is available in this record (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study implements a task (PASAT) requiring rule-based arithmetic operations and sequencing consistent with problem-solving (I5). It includes a whole-brain, group-level task effect in healthy adults (Analysis 14505331_analysis_0: PASAT>REPEAT, whole-brain, random-effects one-sample t-test; I6). Results are reported in Talairach coordinates (I7) and BOLD signal was the measured outcome (I8). Coordinate results are provided in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), healthy-group task effects are present, and this is empirical human fMRI data. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive (transitive) reasoning using acoustically presented problems, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (logical operations, goal-directed inference). It reports whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants (n=12), uses BOLD measurement, and provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach with peak tables and cluster-corrected thresholds. All inclusion criteria are therefore satisfied (I5–I9). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a mental arithmetic task that entails goal-directed, rule-based calculation (meets I5). It includes whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses in healthy adult participants (twin sample) (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and uses BOLD as the measured signal (I8). Voxelwise/coordinate results are reported (peaks and tables), satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain effects are present (not ROI-only), the study is empirical and reports healthy-group task effects, and it is not restricted to disease/age/gender comparisons. Full text appears available in the provided record. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

This PET study used a mental arithmetic task (arithmetic addition) that meets the review's problem-solving definition and reports whole-brain rCBF voxelwise results in MNI coordinates (reported peaks). However, the NeuroStore extraction shows only between-group genotype contrasts (SL+LL > SS) and does not report any within-healthy-group task>baseline or task-related activation contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts / lacks healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (problem-solving arithmetic task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (MNI coordinates reported), I8 (rCBF measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: none additionally beyond those listed. Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to E5.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment of diagnostic reasoning (reading clinical stems, selecting diagnoses, reflecting) that operationalizes goal-directed problem solving and critical thinking processes (meets I5). NeuroStore extraction indicates voxelwise peaks reported in Table 1 (reported peaks listed), satisfying the requirement for stereotactic coordinate results (I7) and acceptable reporting in tables (I9). Thresholding and reported peaks indicate task-related increases were tested and reported. No exclusion criteria apply based on the provided document. Full text is available in this NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Confidence moderate-high due to reliance on the NeuroStore extract for presence of coordinate table.

The task involves logical reasoning in legal decision-making (evaluating vignettes and rating responsibility/punishment), which fits the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed evaluation and application of rule-based judgments). The study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI contrasts (model fit and inference over whole brain) in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 18–45). BOLD signal is the measure reported, coordinate space is Talairach, and stereotactic peak coordinates are provided in tables. Voxelwise results are thresholded (FDR) and reported in tables (Table 1–4). There is no indication the results are ROI-only or limited to between-group/disease comparisons. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study investigates planning/goal-directed navigation in healthy adults using task-based fMRI and models of planning vs. TD learning. It includes multiple whole-brain, group-level analyses (GLM one-sample t-tests) with reported stereotactic peaks in MNI space and BOLD measures. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

The task is a mental rotation (identical vs mirror judgment of hands/tools) and does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5): it involves spatial transformation/visual comparison rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations within a rule set to reach a solution. The study does satisfy I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables).
