The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of fluid reasoning using 3×3 matrix serial reasoning items (NNAT-adapted) that require goal-directed problem solving (select correct answer from five alternatives), meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. Thresholding and multiple-comparison correction are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy task effects). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

The study used the Tower of London task, a canonical problem-solving/planning paradigm (I5). The study investigated working memory for allocentric vs egocentric spatial recall in healthy adults using task-based fMRI (BOLD), but it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem-solving, planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses, n=20, second-level random effects), I7 (results reported in MNI coordinate space with reported peaks), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported). The study used a task-based PET mental arithmetic (serial subtraction) task that fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed arithmetic operations and rule-based processing), satisfying I5. The study uses a task-based PET (H2(15)O) Tower of London planning task, which is a canonical problem-solving/planning paradigm (meets I5). The study uses a mental-arithmetic dual-task paradigm that meets the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed, rule-based arithmetic operations requiring planning/solution execution), satisfying I5. Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (reported peaks/tables) and the measured signal is BOLD. Voxelwise results are presented in tables of peaks. All required inclusion criteria are therefore satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study reports a task that explicitly involves reasoning based on episodic memory: subjects performed reasoning, episodic retrieval, and episodic memory–based reasoning tasks that required selecting the correct bottom scene corresponding to a top scene (i.e., evaluating options and deriving the correct match). This is a task-based fMRI study using a semantic judgment task that requires interpretation and application of semantic/quantitative rules (fits the review's problem-solving definition, which includes semantic problem-solving). Results are not ROI-only, and the study presents voxelwise coordinates and BOLD results. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This PET activation study uses the Tower of Toronto task, which meets the review’s definition of problem-solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing under rule constraints). It reports task-related rCBF increases (PET perfusion) and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. Multiple within-group, whole-brain group-level contrasts (cognitive/associative/autonomous phases > reference) are reported for healthy adult participants (older adults; n=12 for within-group analyses; group comparisons use n=24). Coordinate tables of reported peaks are available. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates in MNI), I8 (rCBF/PET measure), and I9 (coordinates reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical data).

The study reports a task requiring participants to use belief and desire information and explicitly manipulates deductive vs. abductive reasoning demands, which involves critical thinking/logic to predict actions—consistent with the review's definition of problem solving (I5). It is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=20) with whole-brain, group-level analyses (model fit/inference over whole brain), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and reports BOLD responses; coordinate tables of peaks are provided—satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), and analyses include within-group task effects in healthy participants. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Meets all inclusion criteria: WCST is a problem-solving/set-shifting task consistent with I5 (goal-directed rule discovery and execution). The study includes whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults (Analysis 23675408_analysis_0; I6). Results are reported in Talairach coordinates with peak tables (I7, I9). Measure is BOLD (functional bold) (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), include healthy within-group task effects (not only between-group), and the paper is empirical. Therefore include.

The study examines clinical reasoning (goal-directed diagnostic problem solving: read stem, select diagnosis, reflect on reasoning), meeting I5. It reports whole-brain voxel-wise GLM group-level analyses (cross-subject regressions) in adult physician participants, satisfying I6. Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space with reported peak tables, satisfying I7 and I9. The measure is BOLD fMRI, satisfying I8. Thresholding and whole-brain inference are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only group comparisons by disease/age/gender, includes healthy adult task effects). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 are met and no exclusions apply.

The study reports a task in which participants read clinical vignettes, select a diagnosis (goal-oriented problem solving) and reflect on reasoning, satisfying the definition of problem solving (I5). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses with reported stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I6, I7) and BOLD as the measured outcome (I8). Coordinate peaks are provided in tables (I9). Thresholding and inference were whole-brain. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes within-group task effects, not a review).

This study reports a cross-subject voxelwise PET-FDG correlation between BMI and baseline prefrontal metabolism in 21 healthy adults (whole-brain model fit). It does not provide a task-related problem-solving contrast: the extracted analysis is a baseline metabolism correlation (task listed as passive viewing of nature cards), not a problem-solving manipulation. Although the abstract mentions a separate cognitive stimulation (numerical calculations) condition, the provided NeuroStore extraction contains only the baseline BMI correlation analysis and no task-related activation coordinates for a problem-solving contrast. It also uses PET metabolic rate (FDG), not BOLD or rCBF. Therefore it meets inclusion I6 (whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults) but does not meet I5 (problem-solving task), I7 (task-related stereotactic activation results), or I8 (BOLD or rCBF). It therefore violates exclusion E5 (does not include any healthy-group task effect). Full text is complete in this record.

The study uses a mental arithmetic task (goal-directed, rule-based operations to obtain correct sums), which meets the review's definition of problem-solving (I5). It is an empirical PET study measuring regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) (I8) in healthy adult participants (n=11 males) and reports whole-brain model fits and group-level contrasts between task conditions (LC>HC and HC>LC), satisfying whole-brain group analysis requirement (I6). Stereotactic coordinates are indicated as MNI and peaks/tables are reported (I7, I9). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not limited to disease/age/gender group comparisons, and include healthy-group task effects. Therefore the article meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I6: the study reports data from a single participant (n=1) and does not provide group-level whole-brain effects in healthy adults. The study does meet I5 (task-based problem solving: calendrical and division tasks), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly met. fulltext_incomplete set to false.

The task is a Moral Judgment Task (moral dilemmas) assessing moral reasoning/decision-making rather than a rule-based, goal-directed problem-solving task as defined in I5. While the study includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI contrasts in healthy adults (random-effects, voxelwise, n=16 healthy controls) and reports BOLD task effects in MNI space with peaks/tables available, it does not involve planning/sequencing actions to reach a correct or rule-defined solution (core of I5). Therefore it fails I5. No exclusion criteria are met.

NeuroStore indicates inference and reported peaks are restricted to pre-defined ROIs using Monte-Carlo small-volume correction (AlphaSim), and all reported results are ROI-based. Therefore the study reports only ROI results (exclusion E3) and does not provide whole-brain group-level voxelwise inference required by I6. The study does meet other inclusions: it is a task-based fMRI study of logical/transitive problem solving (I5), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI (I7), uses BOLD measures (I8), and provides voxelwise results reported in extracted peaks (I9). Full text is available via the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: (I5) Task involves mental arithmetic (subtraction problems), which qualifies as problem solving under the review definition (goal-directed operations applying rules to arrive at a correct solution). (I6) Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; n=209 healthy adults). (I7) Results reported in MNI stereotactic space with reported peaks. (I8) Uses BOLD functional measure. (I9) Voxelwise results (peaks) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), they report within-group task effects in healthy adults, and the paper is empirical. Therefore include.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=11) using a problem-solving task (trial-and-error search for correct stimulus), meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. Analyses are whole-brain with group-level within-subject contrasts and whole-brain inference. Results are reported in MNI space with peak coordinates/tables, and the measure is BOLD signal. Reported results appear in tables (reported peaks), satisfying acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group only, not disease/age/gender comparisons, and is empirical).

The reported task is a numerosity/magnitude comparison (participants indicate numerosity of dot displays), which is a perceptual/numeric judgment and does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (requires a goal-directed problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing or critical-thinking operations to reach a solution). The study does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults, n=16), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space with peaks), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study examines a problem-solving task (Chinese Remote Associates Test) using task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD coordinate results in MNI space; however, the NeuroStore record shows only a between-group contrast (IBMT > RT) for the solution condition and no within-group/task-related effects for healthy participants. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (study reports only between-group contrasts or lacks any healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (problem-solving task: Chinese RAT), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (MNI coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD measure), I9 (coordinates available). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text is complete in the provided record.

The task is a deductive/relational reasoning (logical inference) task that involves rule-based problem solving (logical operations), satisfying definition of problem solving. The study used task-based fMRI (BOLD) in healthy adults (n=15) with whole-brain group-level analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI152, and reports peak results. Thresholding and mixed-effects GLM are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not group-comparison-only, empirical, includes healthy-group task effects).

The study examines imagined navigation between named start and target locations with explicit instructions to plan routes (e.g., take a longer route if the direct route would be too short), which involves setting a goal and planning/sequencing actions to reach it — meeting the review's problem-solving definition (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI activation maps in healthy adults (n=10) with inference over the whole brain (I6). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space with tables of peak coordinates (I7, I9). The measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), the study includes healthy-group task effects (not only between-group comparisons), and it is empirical human neuroimaging. Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study uses a task that meets the review's definition of problem solving (route optimization and planning), reports group-level random-effects analyses, BOLD measure, and stereotactic coordinates (MNI). However, NeuroStore indicates that inference was restricted to a region of interest for all reported analyses, i.e., only ROI-based inference/results are reported despite model fitting over the whole brain. This triggers exclusion E3 (reports only ROI results) and means the study does not satisfy I6 (at least one whole-brain group-level analysis reported). Inclusion IDs met: I5, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion ID not met: I6. Therefore the study is excluded.

This task-based fMRI study tested Chinese chess checkmate problem solving (clear goal-directed problem-solving requiring planning/sequence operations) in healthy adult participants. It reports multiple whole-brain, group-level task analyses (one-sample t-tests with model fit and inference over whole brain for within-group task effects) and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (reported peaks/tables). BOLD signal was used and coordinates are reported in tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD/rCBF measure), and I9 (coordinates available in tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is available from the NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of mental arithmetic verification (a goal-directed, rule-based problem-solving task) in healthy adults. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (model fit over whole brain, one-sample t-tests), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with reported peak tables, and uses BOLD as the measured signal. Voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults (n=30). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only contrast, not non-empirical). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and the study should be included.

This study does not meet the review’s scope for problem-solving (I5). The task is a moral judgment/dilemma task (agree/disagree with proposed solutions) rather than a defined problem-solving paradigm involving planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to reach a correct solution. The document does not report any within-group whole-brain task effect for healthy controls; only patient within-group effects and between-group (HC>ASD or interactions) contrasts are reported. Thus it lacks a clear healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I6 not met) and effectively presents between-group contrasts without healthy-group-only task coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (MNI coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (coordinate results available). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only between-group contrasts for healthy group task effects / no healthy-group task effect reported). Full text appears complete for the NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses a Tower of London task, which is a canonical problem-solving/planning task involving a goal, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based moves (meets I5). The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain model fit and reports within-group contrast results for the healthy control group (n=18), satisfying I6. Results are reported in MNI space (I7) and the measured signal is BOLD (I8). Coordinate/peak results are listed (reported peaks: 13 for controls), satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), healthy-group task effects are reported (not only between-group differences), and the paper reports original empirical data. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task is perceptual spatial judgments (allocentric/egocentric position and luminance discrimination of a virtual fork), which does not involve goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing actions, or critical thinking to derive novel solutions. The document does satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI with healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analyses), and I9 (coordinates reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no patient-group-only contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore exclusion is due solely to failure to meet I5.

This study does not meet the review’s core task requirement (I5). The task is autobiographical reasoning/reflecting on personal memories, not a problem-solving task involving a goal plus requirement to figure out/planning/sequencing operations under a rule set to reach a solution. The study does meet other methodological criteria: I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults: whole-brain model fit, n=24), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (voxelwise peaks reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes within-group task effects in healthy adults). Therefore exclude for failure to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation using a mental arithmetic (serial subtraction) task that requires goal-directed operations and sequential rule-based calculation, satisfying the review definition of problem solving (I5). Analyses were performed as whole-brain group-level tests in healthy adults (n=8) with one-sample tests and whole-brain inference reported, meeting I6. Results are reported as stereotactic Talairach coordinates with peak tables, meeting I7 and I9. The measured outcome is BOLD signal, satisfying I8. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI analyses, is empirical, and contains within-group task effects. Therefore the study is included.

Excluded because the reported analyses are region-of-interest only (model fit over region of interest; region-level thresholding focused on left IPL), which meets exclusion E3. This study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task = mental arithmetic, a rule-based problem-solving task), I7 (results reported in MNI coordinate space), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (coordinate peaks reported in tables). However it does NOT meet I6 because no whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis is reported. Full text is available in the provided record (not incomplete).

The study reports event-related fMRI of a planning/problem-solving task (Tower of Hanoi adaptation) in healthy adults (n=8, ages 18–32). Analysis used whole-brain voxelwise regression and reports task-related BOLD increases as stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) in tables (multiple peak coordinates listed). Thus it meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: a task-defined problem-solving paradigm (planning operations), whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults, stereotactic coordinate reporting, BOLD measure, and coordinate tables are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not limited to group comparisons, and is empirical).

The study reports an event-related, task-based fMRI mental arithmetic (multiplication verification) paradigm that fits the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed arithmetic operations using rule-based procedures) (I5). Analyses include whole-brain random-effects GLM with model fit and inference over the whole brain in a healthy adult sample (n=20) (I6). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space with peaks/tables (I7,I9). The measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). The NeuroStore record indicates within-group task effects (difficulty contrast D>E) rather than ROI-only or patient-group-only comparisons, and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is INCLUDED.

The study uses a mental arithmetic (problem-solving) task and reports whole-brain BOLD results in Talairach space (meets I5, I7, I8, I9). However, participants are not healthy adults (patients and controls are adolescents/children; mean age 14.4, range 7.1–24.4), so it does not include group-level effects in healthy adults (fails I6). The extracted results show within-group effects reported for the patient (TS) group but no within-group healthy adult control task effect; most reported contrasts are between-group (disease vs control), so it meets exclusion criterion E5 (includes only between-group contrasts or lacks any healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded from this review.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task (I5 not met): the task is emotion/food-picture processing with a one-back repetition detection, not goal-directed problem solving. Although whole-brain analyses are reported, they are omnibus between-group contrasts comparing obese, RYGB and normal-weight women and do not report a healthy-group task effect (I6 not met). The report does include stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD measures (I7, I8) and coordinates/results availability is acceptable (I9). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only disease-related group comparisons are presented) and E5 (results are only between-group contrasts/no healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study is excluded.

The task is the Alternate Uses Task (divergent thinking), which does not meet the review’s definition of problem solving (I5) because it is open-ended creativity generation rather than goal-directed rule-based planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct or constrained solution. The paper does include whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adults (I6, I7, I8) and reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI (I7); voxelwise results are reported (I9). However, NeuroStore-extracted analyses are all reported as between-group contrasts/cross-subject regressions with no clear within-healthy-group task effect, meaning the study appears to report only between-group contrasts (E5). Therefore it must be excluded.

Exclusion E5 met: the paper does not report a whole-brain, group-level task activation map specifically for healthy adults. While it includes whole-brain ICA and GLM results, these are either across combined patients+controls or reported as between-group contrasts (healthy vs schizophrenia). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/maps). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level effect reported for healthy adults alone), I5 (task does not clearly meet the review's problem-solving definition as a cognitive problem-solving task; it is a spatial navigation/allocentric learning task and the document does not explicitly frame it as problem-solving). Therefore the study is excluded under E5.

Exclusion E5 applies: the NeuroStore extract reports only between-group contrasts (patient vs controls) and simple between-group effects; no within-healthy-group task activations are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates are available in reported peaks/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is semantic/category and perceptual number decisions — not clearly a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no whole-brain, group-level task effect reported specifically for healthy adult participants independent of between-group contrasts). fulltext_incomplete=false

The study investigates false-belief (Theory of Mind) and response inhibition (Go/No-Go), not goal-directed problem-solving as defined in inclusion criterion I5. While it meets other technical criteria (whole-brain random-effects fMRI group analysis in healthy adults with BOLD measures and MNI coordinates reported), the tasks do not involve identifying and performing problem-solving processes (planning/sequencing actions to reach a solution). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) apply.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD coordinate results (Talairach) and group-level contrasts (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), the experimental task involves forced-choice perceptual/social-judgement decisions about relative social hierarchy, alliance, age, gender, fame and a baseline numerical task. These judgments do not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a novel/correct solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of mental arithmetic (96 single- and two-digit addition problems), which constitutes a rule-based problem-solving task (I5). Analyses were fitted over the whole brain with group-level, within-group parametric modulation effects in healthy adults (n=16) and reported stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (reported peaks/tables), using BOLD measures (I6–I8). Voxelwise results are reported in tables (supplementary/main), satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), involve healthy-group task effects (not only between-group or clinical comparisons), and are empirical. Full text appears available in the record.

The study uses an event-related task requiring logical/deontic reasoning (judging whether a person could have broken a rule), which qualifies as problem solving involving evaluation and rule-based operations (meets I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level second-level analyses in healthy adults (n=24) with inference over the whole brain (meets I6). Results are reported as stereotactic peaks in MNI space (meets I7) and the measured signal is BOLD functional response (meets I8). Voxelwise results are reported as coordinate tables/peaks (meets I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects). Full text is available in the NeuroStore record provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults (n=16, mean age 24.5) using a mental arithmetic task requiring goal-directed problem solving (produce multiplication solutions and use them in subsequent operations), which meets the review’s problem-solving definition (evaluating/planning/sequencing operations under rule-based arithmetic). The fMRI analysis is a whole-brain, group-level random-effects parametric modulation (model fit over whole brain) reporting BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (Table I peaks). Voxelwise results are reported in a table of coordinates. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete in the provided record.

The study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). It is a Theory of Mind false/true belief task assessing belief reasoning about others’ perspectives, not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm requiring planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to reach a solution. It does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic (MNI) coordinates (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and provides voxelwise results in reported tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., results are not ROI-only and include within-group healthy task effects). Therefore excluded for failure to meet I5.

This is an event-related fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task in healthy adults (n=24) reporting BOLD activations. Analyses were whole-brain (model fit over: whole brain) with second-level random-effects ANOVA and reported stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (peaks in Table 3). The task clearly involves planning/problem-solving (goal-directed sequencing and evaluation). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (BOLD) using the Wason Selection Task, a logical problem-solving paradigm requiring rule evaluation and selection, matching the review definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with results given in MNI coordinates (reported peaks/tables) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., Social Contracts > Precautions, Stories > Rest). Participants are healthy adults (n=12). Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (task-based fMRI problem solving; whole-brain group results; stereotactic coordinates in MNI; BOLD measure; voxelwise results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports a Tower of London planning task (a canonical problem-solving/planning paradigm) using task-based BOLD fMRI. It includes whole-brain, group-level within-group contrasts (planning > baseline) for the low-OCS group (Analysis 18342423_analysis_0, n=12) and for the high-OCS group, so there are healthy-group task effects available. Coordinate space is MNI and NeuroStore reports stereotactic peaks/tables, satisfying coordinate reporting. BOLD measure is explicitly listed. The low-OCS group is described as having no members meeting OCD criteria (two with subthreshold symptoms), so the within-group low-OCS analysis qualifies as a healthy adult group-level whole-brain effect for inclusion. The study is not ROI-only and does not report only between-group contrasts. Therefore I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does not meet I5: the task is moral decision-making/theory-of-mind evaluation using everyday moral conflict stories, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing/executing rule-based operations to reach a correct or more appropriate previously unknown solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults are reported), I7 (results reported in MNI coordinate space), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported as peak coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is available in the provided record.

The task examines referential ambiguity/resolution during sentence comprehension; the authors explicitly interpret referential ambiguity as engaging “problem-solving to select a unique referent,” meeting the review’s broad definition of problem solving (goal: determine referent; need: figure out referent via inferencing/resolution). The study is task-based fMRI in healthy adults (n=22), uses BOLD, reports whole-brain, group-level random effects analyses with reported stereotactic peaks in MNI space, and provides coordinate tables. Thresholding and reported peaks confirm voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes within-group healthy task effects, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study is includable for the meta-analysis.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of probabilistic reasoning/decision making under uncertainty that requires subjects to evaluate evidence and choose between alternatives—consistent with problem-solving defined as evaluative and inferential processes to reach a goal. It includes whole-brain voxelwise fixed-effects analyses and whole-brain inference, reports BOLD measures, and provides stereotactic (Talairach) peak coordinates in a table. Participants are healthy adults (n=8). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy within-group task contrasts). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study does not meet the review objective of problem-solving tasks (I5 not met): the task is a card-guessing gambling task, not a problem-solving paradigm. The reported analyses are between-group contrasts (controls > pathological gamblers) with no within-healthy-group task effect reported, so it violates exclusion E5 (includes only between-group contrasts / no healthy-group task effect) and fails to satisfy I6 (no whole-brain group-level healthy-task effect documented). It does meet I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI reported), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure reported), and I9 (coordinates/results reported). Full text appears accessible in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly used a goal-directed problem-solving task (participants simulated solving specific problems in imagined scenarios), meeting the review definition of problem solving. The paper reports group-level second-level random-effects whole-brain GLM analyses (and ROI analyses) in healthy adults (n=29, mean age 22.4). Results are reported in MNI space with peak coordinates/tables and the measured signal is BOLD. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Study includes a Tower of London planning task that meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing actions), satisfying I5. Analyses are task-based fMRI with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference reported at group level in healthy adult participants (I6). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with peaks listed in tables (I7, I9). Measure is BOLD (I8). The paper is empirical, not ROI-only, and reports within-group task effects for healthy adults, so no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of mental arithmetic (a problem-solving task involving rule-based operations and selection of correct solutions), reports group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses, uses BOLD as the measured signal, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with tables of peak activations. Participants are healthy adults (n=24). Although the abstract mentions ROI analyses, the NeuroStore extraction explicitly lists whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and tables of peaks, so the study is not limited to ROI results. All inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using BOLD contrast (measure: bold response) that examines goal-directed reasoning in a competitive 'beauty contest' game (and also a mental multiplication task). The tasks require problem-solving processes (goal-directed strategic reasoning, planning/evaluating others’ choices, and arithmetic operations), meeting I5. Several analyses report whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adult participants (n up to 20) with reported peaks and model fits over the whole brain, satisfying I6. Coordinate space is MNI and peaks are reported, satisfying I7. BOLD measure is explicitly reported, satisfying I8. Reported peaks/coordinates are available in the extracted results, satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes within-group task effects in healthy adults; empirical original data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study uses an event-related fMRI Raven's Progressive Matrices reasoning task that requires deducing and applying sequencing rules, meeting the review's problem-solving definition. It reports whole-brain group-level analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain; one-sample GLM) in healthy adults (n=19, mean age 21). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with tables of peaks, and the measure is BOLD signal. Thresholding and peaks are listed. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, empirical, includes healthy task effects). Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of mental arithmetic (two-digit × one-digit multiplication) that fits the definition of problem solving (goal-directed calculation using rule-based operations). It used healthy adult participants (n=16) and reports a whole-brain, group-level random-effects contrast (task blocks > rest) with inference over the whole brain. Results are reported in MNI space and the measured modality is BOLD fMRI. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only or patient comparison, and is empirical).

The reported task is a perceptual discrimination (classify two hands by number of raised fingers, palm orientation, or thumb color) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5. The task does not require goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions, or executing operations to reach a previously unknown solution; it is a magnitude/feature classification. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults are reported), I7 (results reported in MNI coordinates/peaks), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported as peaks). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I5 (does not examine a problem-solving task).

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of deductive/relational reasoning (logical, rule-based problem solving), meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. It includes whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects group analyses (FLAME) in healthy adult participants (n=24; also subgroup n=12 reported), reports BOLD measures, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with reported peaks. Thresholding and inference were whole-brain. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, and includes healthy-group task effects).

Excluded because the reported analyses used a searchlight approach but inference was explicitly restricted to a region-of-interest with small-volume correction (SVC); therefore the paper reports ROI-limited results rather than whole-brain group-level effects (meets exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD/functional measure reported), I9 (voxelwise/searchlight results are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level inference reported — inference restricted to ROI/SVC), I5 (the task is a spatial navigation goal-direction judgment; although it involves goal direction representation and may relate to route planning, the report describes directional judgements rather than an explicit problem-solving task as defined by I5). Full text was available in the provided record and no access issues were indicated.

This study is excluded because its reported analyses are limited to region-of-interest (hV5/MT) results rather than whole-brain, violating inclusion criterion I6 and triggering exclusion E3. Although it is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and coordinate reporting is acceptable, the task (mental/visual rotation) is a visuospatial perception task and the document does not provide evidence that it meets the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Therefore: Exclusion criterion met: E3. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (Talairach coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (coordinate reporting acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis). Full text is complete for screening.

The study uses a Stroop Color-Word task (cognitive control/conflict), not a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met). Although it reports whole-brain BOLD analyses and stereotactic coordinates in MNI (I7, I8, I9 met), all reported results are between-group contrasts comparing cocaine patients and healthy controls with no within-group task-related effects reported for healthy adults. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E5 (only between-group contrasts / no healthy-group task effect) and effectively meets E4 (reports disease-related group comparisons only). Conclusion: EXCLUDED.

The study uses a PET receptor-binding measure ([(11)C]FLB-457 BPND) during the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task, which qualifies as a problem-solving/executive task (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in healthy adults (within-group correlations) (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and allows voxelwise results in reported peaks/tables (I9). However, it does NOT report BOLD or regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) measures (it reports molecular receptor binding), so it fails inclusion criterion I8. Therefore it must be excluded. Note: some task contrasts had inference restricted to ROIs, but the primary reason for exclusion is the absence of BOLD/rCBF imaging data (I8 not met).

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning paradigm (meets I5). It reports whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space (meets I7) using BOLD fMRI (meets I8) and coordinate tables (meets I9). However, all extracted analyses are reported for participants characterized as patients/high-risk for obsessive-compulsive symptoms and focus on between-group contrasts (high vs low risk; concordant/discordant pairs). There is no clearly reported whole-brain, group-level task activation effect in healthy adult individuals (criterion I6 not met). Because the paper only reports between-group contrasts and does not present healthy-group task effects, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Therefore the study is excluded.

The study investigates false belief and counterfactual reasoning (theory-of-mind/social inference) using event-related BOLD fMRI in healthy adults, with whole-brain analyses and MNI coordinates reported. However, it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no explicit goal-directed problem to be solved via planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a correct/previously unknown solution). Tasks are social inference questions about beliefs or hypothetical alternatives rather than domain-general problem solving. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met, though I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The paper includes a problem-solving task (Tower of London) and reports BOLD results in MNI space (I5, I8, I7, I9 satisfied). However, the TOL (problem-solving) results are reported within a region-of-interest framework (no whole-brain TOL activation reported), and the study mainly reports between-genotype group contrasts rather than a whole-brain task effect in healthy adults. Therefore it does not provide a whole-brain, group-level activation for the problem-solving task (I6 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts / no healthy-group task effect reported).

The study uses a false-belief (theory-of-mind) task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based problem solving). Although it meets other methodological criteria, it does not investigate problem-solving across domains and therefore does not address the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level BOLD analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD measure), I9 (voxelwise/peak results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). I7 (stereotactic coordinates) is not explicitly reported in the NeuroStore record. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The task requires participants to decide (goal) whether concept–feature sentences are true or false, involving evaluative/ reasoning processes (authors interpret false-verification as finding/evaluating contradictions), which fits the review's operational definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI results in healthy adults (n=21) (I6), provides coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD responses (I8), and voxelwise results are reported (I9). Thresholding and inference are whole-brain FWE-corrected. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy within-group task effects).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD coordinate results (Talairach) and voxelwise peaks, so it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the task is a numerical size-congruity/number comparison task (judging which of two number words is numerically larger), which is a perceptual/cognitive comparison paradigm rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a novel solution). Therefore I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports an event-related mental-arithmetic (multiplication) task that involves goal-directed problem solving (solve multiplication problems using arithmetic rules), meeting I5. It includes group-level whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=20), meeting I6. Results are reported in MNI space with reported peak coordinates/tables, meeting I7 and I9. The measure is BOLD fMRI, meeting I8. No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain (not ROI only), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons, and include within-group task effects in healthy adults. Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports a mental rotation (visuospatial) task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no evidence of goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing, or rule-based operations to reach a novel solution). It does, however, include a whole-brain, task-based BOLD analysis in healthy adults with reported MNI coordinates (peaks in tables). Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied but I5 (task is problem solving) is not. No exclusion criteria from the review are met.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (task is spatial mental-rotation/imagery of self-rotation rather than a problem-solving task as defined). The abstract and extracted task describe imagined self-rotation and updating object positions (spatial transformation/imagery), not goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or rule-based solution-finding across domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain analyses with group-level effects reported: group t-tests and reported peaks), I7 (coordinates reported in Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Exclusion criteria met: none. Therefore excluded due to failure to satisfy I5.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of algebraic problem solving (event-related mental arithmetic with 214 two-step equations), meeting the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed algebraic operations and execution). It reports whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference with group-level effects in healthy adults (n=15, mean age 24.6), and lists stereotactic coordinate peaks in Talairach (Table tbl1). The measure is BOLD response. Coordinates/results are reported in the paper (table). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes within-group task effects in healthy adults; is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses the Wason Selection Task, a logical/problem-solving task involving rule evaluation and selection of actions to test a rule, meeting I5. It reports group-level whole-brain analyses (analyses 1–4 model fit over whole brain; random- and cross-subject effects), satisfying I6. Coordinate space is MNI and peaks are reported in tables, meeting I7 and I9. The measure is BOLD (functional bold), satisfying I8. Although ROI analyses are reported, whole-brain voxelwise results are also provided, so E3 (ROI-only) does not apply. Participants are healthy adults (N=16). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the requirement of studying healthy adult humans. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task is a problem-solving/set-shifting modified Wisconsin Card Sorting Test), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise peak coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (participants are macaque monkeys, n=2, not healthy adult humans), I7 (coordinates reported in bicommissural space, not Talairach or MNI). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain task-based fMRI/PET in healthy adults.

This fMRI study examines false vs true belief reasoning (Theory of Mind) using a Sally-Anne cartoon task. Although it is a task-based BOLD fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and coordinate tables (satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9), it does not study a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The tasks involve attributing beliefs/perspective-taking rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing actions to reach a goal, or applying rule-based operations to derive solutions. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) results (E3). While the task involves goal-directed navigation that can be construed as problem-solving (I5 met), and the paper reports BOLD analyses in MNI space with peak coordinates (I7, I8, I9 met), it does not include any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task analysis (I6 not met). All reported model fits and inferences are restricted to striatal ROIs. Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one whole-brain group-level analysis and must be excluded.

The study reports a task in which healthy adult participants (n=15, mean age 22.14) performed a goal-directed creative design task (designing book cover illustrations) that required generation and evaluation of solutions, consistent with problem-solving processes (goal formation, idea generation, and evaluative critical thinking). It used task-based fMRI with BOLD measurement and group random-effects whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain), reporting stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables of activation peaks for generate>evaluate and evaluate>generate). Thresholding and peak tables are provided. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task involving goal-directed problem-solving/idea generation and evaluation), I6 (whole-brain, group-level, healthy adults), I7 (MNI coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (results available in tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study investigates spatial updating/mental rotation and memory for object locations rather than an explicit problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing to reach a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (does not probe a problem-solving task per the review definition; task is spatial memory/imagery/updating rather than planning/sequencing to solve a novel problem). No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., results are whole-brain, not ROI-only; healthy-group task effects present). Full text is available in the record. Therefore EXCLUDED.

The task involves hypothesis testing/category induction with an explicit goal (learn which batteries are charged) and requires generating, evaluating, and updating hypotheses — consistent with problem solving as defined (I5). The study used whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM analyses in healthy adults (n=17) (I6). Results report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space with tables of peak activations (I7, I9). The measured signal is BOLD fMRI (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), study is empirical and reports within-group task effects in healthy adults. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusions.

This study investigates spatial route learning/navigation (encoding of landmark views and movements) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no evidence the task required goal-directed problem solving involving evaluating, planning/sequencing actions or applying rule-based operations to find a solution). It does meet other inclusion criteria: reports group-level whole-brain analyses (model fit over whole brain), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI (I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only). Therefore EXCLUDED because I5 is not satisfied.

The study reports task-based fMRI BOLD results from healthy adult participants performing deductive/relational reasoning and rule-based reasoning tasks that meet the problem-solving definition (goal-directed, rule-based operations). Analyses were whole-brain with group-level mixed-effects models, inference over the whole brain, and reported stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (reported peaks/tables). Voxelwise results are available in tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

All inclusion criteria are met. The study used a task-based perfusion fMRI (rCBF) paradigm involving serial subtraction (mental arithmetic), which qualifies as a problem-solving task (goal-directed arithmetic operations within a rule set). Analyses were whole-brain GLMs with group-level, cross-subject regressions (model fit over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=23). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (reported peaks). Thus it reports task-related rCBF increases with coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not only between-group or clinical comparisons). Full text appears available in the provided record.

The task in this study is magnitude estimation/mapping (placing numeric or brightness probes on a reference line), which does not meet the review's definition of problem solving (I5: goal-directed critical thinking/planning/sequencing to arrive at a solution). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI (I6), reports Talairach coordinates (I7), uses BOLD (I8), and reports voxelwise results in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I5.

The study uses the Tower of London planning task, a canonical problem-solving paradigm (goal-directed planning/sequencing) and reports whole-brain, group-level (second-level random-effects) BOLD results for healthy adult controls. Coordinates are reported in Talairach space (reported peaks/tables). Therefore it satisfies the review’s task definition and imaging/data reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy within-group task effects, is empirical).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) The task is a problem-solving math task (algebra-like pyramid problems requiring planning and execution of solution strategies). (I6) Analyses are whole-brain with group-level effects (model fit and inference over whole brain; reported group peaks; n=36 healthy adults). (I7) Results reported in Talairach stereotactic space with coordinate peaks. (I8) Measure is BOLD fMRI (functional bold). (I9) Voxelwise results are reported in tables of coordinates (reported peaks in Table). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task effects in healthy adults. Thresholding and reported peaks support inclusion.

This study does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task manipulates belief- and desire-valence in Theory of Mind (false/true belief and desire valence) to probe neural networks supporting mental-state reasoning and self-perspective inhibition; it is not described as a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm involving planning/sequencing actions or executing operations to reach a solution as required by I5. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports coordinates in MNI space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and voxelwise results are reported (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the paper is excluded for failing to satisfy I5 (problem-solving requirement).

This study was excluded because it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). The experimental task probes spatial memory and imagined orientations relative to an extrinsic reference frame, not goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or rule-based operations to reach a solution. The study does satisfy other inclusion criteria: whole-brain, task-based fMRI with group-level effects in healthy adults (I6); reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7); uses BOLD fMRI measures (I8); and voxelwise results are available as reported coordinates/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., ROI-only results or patient-group-only contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none.

The experimental task is VR exploration/memorization for spatial navigation and memory, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed critical thinking/planning/sequencing to arrive at a solution). The study does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fixed-effects analysis), I7 (reports Talairach stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (reported peaks in a table). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails I5. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8, I9. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5.)

Excluded because the reported analyses are ROI-based only (model fit over: region of interest; planned comparisons on seven ROIs), which meets exclusion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results reported in Talairach stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure reported), and I9 (stereotactic peak coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not clearly meet our definition of a problem-solving task — it is a moral judgment/dilemma task, not planning/sequencing to reach a goal), and I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis reported; only ROI analyses). Full text is available in the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study meets the review criteria: tasks include rule-based, goal-directed decisions (magnitude comparison to 5 and parity judgment), which fall under the I5 definition of operations that execute rules/logical operations to arrive at correct responses. The study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (n=16) (I6). Results are reported in Talairach stereotactic space with tables of peak coordinates (I7, I9). The neuroimaging measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: analyses are whole-brain (not only ROIs), healthy-group task effects are reported, and this is empirical human data. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: the task is diagnostic reasoning/MCQ answering (a problem-solving task involving goal-directed evaluation and selection of answers), it reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit over: whole brain) in healthy adult participants (board-certified physicians, n=15), reports BOLD responses, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with reported peak coordinates (Table 1). Voxelwise results are available and thresholding is reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy-task effects). Full text appears accessible via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (n=17) using a stepwise category induction task that requires finding an invariant attribute across stimuli (a goal with the need to determine a solution strategy), which fits the review's definition of problem solving. The paper provides whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (GLM and PPI) with reported stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space and BOLD measures. Results include whole-brain inference and tables of reported peaks. Therefore it satisfies I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates, Talairach), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (results reported as peaks/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This study does not meet the review's problem-solving task requirement (I5). The tasks are reality evaluation (real vs. unreal judgments) and recognition (old/new memory), which are perceptual/recognition/memory tasks and do not involve goal-directed problem solving, planning or rule-based operations as defined. Additionally, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group contrasts (Control > Schizophrenia) and does not report healthy-group task effects or within-healthy-group task activations, so exclusion criterion E5 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only between-group contrasts / no healthy-group task effect reported). Full text is complete in the provided NeuroStore record.

The study reports a task in which participants infer and apply rules to classify symbol strings (rule-learning task with sample blocks, feedback, and application to new strings), which fits the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed rule inference and execution). It includes whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults (n=16) with second-level ANOVAs and voxelwise inference reported across the whole brain. Results are given in MNI stereotactic space with reported peaks and table entries. The imaging measure is BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are reported (FDR voxel-level; reported peaks and Table tbl1). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only or non-empirical paper). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses an event-related task requiring quantitative/problem-solving (deciding perimeters under congruent vs. incongruent conditions), meeting I5. It reports BOLD fMRI measures (I8), group-level whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference in healthy adults (n=14) (I6). Coordinates are given in MNI space with reported peaks/tables (I7) and results are present in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy task effects). Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive/relational reasoning (syllogisms) in healthy adults that meets all inclusion criteria. I5: The task requires goal-directed logical evaluation and application of rules (critical thinking/problem solving). I6: Multiple analyses were fit and tested over the whole brain with group-level effects in n=19 healthy adults. I7: Results are reported in MNI stereotactic space with reported peak coordinates. I8: The measured outcome is BOLD (functional bold response). I9: Voxelwise results are reported (reported peaks; thresholding and whole-brain inference specified). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only contrast, not a review). Therefore the study is included for the meta-analysis.

The study examines planning using the Tower of London (a problem-solving task involving goal decomposition and sequencing), reports a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level fMRI analysis (Analysis 23911779_analysis_0: whole-brain model fit and whole-brain FWE voxel-level inference), uses BOLD as the measure, provides coordinates in MNI space, and tests healthy adult participants (n=52). These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply (results are not limited to ROIs, the sample is healthy adults, and the paper is empirical).

Primary exclusion: The reported tasks are spatial memory/mental imagery and viewpoint-transformation/pointing tasks (REF, ROT, JRD) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed operations requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing under an explicit rule set to reach a solution). While the study meets other methodological criteria (whole-brain random-effects GLM in healthy adults; Talairach coordinates; BOLD measure; voxelwise results reported), it does not assess the type of problem solving required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group effects in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in Talairach), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm per provided definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I5 - task-based fMRI of problem solving (two-digit addition/subtraction with rule-based evaluation of correctness); I6 - whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults (n=32); I7 - reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach with peak tables; I8 - BOLD measure reported; I9 - voxelwise results are reported in tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only group comparisons, includes healthy task effects, empirical). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The study includes a mental arithmetic (calculation) task that fits the review’s definition of problem solving (algebraic/arithmetic operations requiring goal-directed operations and rule-based computation). It reports group-level random-effects BOLD fMRI results in healthy adults (n=10). Several contrasts (e.g. Calculation; Calculation > naming) were analyzed with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (corrected p<0.01, cluster-level; reported peaks in tables), and coordinate space is specified as MNI. Voxelwise results are reported in tables (tbl1, tbl2, tbl3). Therefore it meets I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (voxelwise results available in tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study reports whole-brain, task-based BOLD fMRI results in healthy adults (n=12) with stereotactic MNI coordinates, satisfying criteria for whole-brain group analysis and BOLD reporting. However, the task is a decision-making / reward-choice paradigm (choosing dice arrangements with explicit probabilities and incentives) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed critical thinking involving planning/sequencing operations to derive a solution). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem solving). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Evidence: task description, contrasts A>B and A>C, whole-brain random-effects analyses, MNI coordinates, BOLD measure.

The task (desire–reason dilemma) assesses self-control/resisting impulses rather than problem solving as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning, sequencing, and rule-based operations to derive a correct solution). Therefore I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults, n=32), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measures reported), I9 (results available in tables). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Conclusion: exclude because it does not study a problem-solving task per I5.

The study reports an event-related task requiring multi-digit addition where participants select the closer candidate answer, which constitutes goal-directed problem solving involving algebraic/arithmetic operations (I5). It includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses (model fit over: whole brain; within-group contrasts; n=18 healthy adults) satisfying I6. Results are reported in Talairach space with reported peak coordinates and tables, meeting I7 and I9. The measure is BOLD, satisfying I8. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), involve healthy-group task effects (not only between-group comparisons), and the paper is empirical. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study uses the PASAT, which requires participants to achieve a goal (correctly add consecutive digits) and to execute rule-based arithmetic operations and sequencing, meeting the review's definition of problem solving. It reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (model fit over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=15), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with tabulated peak coordinates, and uses BOLD functional measures. Thresholding and contrasts (ADD>REPEAT; conjunction) are reported voxelwise with FWE correction. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the paper satisfies all required inclusion criteria for this review.

All inclusion criteria are met. The task includes simple and complex arithmetic equation verification, which fits the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed operations conforming to rule sets to arrive at a correct judgment). The study used task-based fMRI with BOLD as the measured signal. A random-effects whole-brain analysis (Analysis 19349235_analysis_0) is reported (p<.05, corrected) with reported Talairach-coordinate peaks in tables, satisfying whole-brain group-level stereotactic reporting. Coordinate results are in Talairach space and peaks are tabulated. Participants are healthy adults (n=17). Although the paper’s primary aim concerns emotion modulation, the arithmetic task qualifies as a problem-solving task for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the reported analyses are limited to a region-of-interest (IPS) rather than whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (study used fMRI/BOLD as indicated by title/abstract and reported peaks), I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results are reported).
