Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates; MNI), I8 (rCBF PET measure), I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported in tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per the review definition). Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5. Full text is complete for screening.

This study is excluded because it reports ROI-restricted inference rather than whole-brain task effects (meets exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results reported in Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), and I9 (peaks/coordinate results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not clearly meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task — it is a reward-based decision-making/switching task rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution), and I6 (no whole-brain group-level inferences reported — inference was restricted to an ROI, so it does not provide whole-brain group effects required). Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record. Therefore excluded on E3 with the above rationale.

This study reports a two-person choice/valuation task varying the number of available options and measures BOLD responses related to option number equality. While it meets several methodological inclusion criteria (I6: includes whole-brain group-level analyses with FWE-corrected voxelwise results; I7: reports MNI coordinates; I8: BOLD measure reported; I9: voxelwise results are reported in tables), it does NOT meet I5. The task is a valuation/decision-making paradigm about equality of choice opportunity, not a problem-solving task as defined (no goal requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a correct or novel solution; reward probability was fixed and choices did not require rule-based problem solving). Therefore the paper should be excluded from the problem-solving meta-analysis.

The task is a Serial Reaction Time Task probing probabilistic sequential learning (procedural/sequence learning), not a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (no evidence of goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/evaluative critical thinking to arrive at solutions). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (MNI stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI measures), and I9 (voxelwise results available). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded because I5 is not met.

This PET study tests a logical reasoning/problem-solving task (falsify conditional logical rules) in healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results in MNI space for rCBF. The task fits the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical reasoning), whole-brain analyses were performed, stereotactic coordinates and peak tables are reported, and rCBF (perfusion) measures are used. Voxelwise within-group task contrasts (post>pre) and conjunction analyses are reported; results are presented as coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes healthy-group task effects).

The task involves rule-based arithmetic manipulation of maintained digits (apply operators indicated by cues and judge probe), which meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed, rule-based operations/planning/execution). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (model fit and inference over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=12). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with peak tables (reported peaks in tbl0005). The measure is BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are thresholded and reported (FDR-corrected p<0.05, voxel-level), satisfying availability of coordinate results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient-group comparisons only, includes within-group healthy task contrasts, empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This study reports BOLD responses (I8), stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and peaks/tables of voxelwise results (I9). However, it does not provide a clear whole-brain, group-level task effect specifically in healthy adult participants (I6 not met). The whole-brain analyses appear to be performed over the combined sample or are not specified as healthy-only; many reported contrasts are between patients and controls. The task is probabilistic decision-making/judgement (JTC), which may not unambiguously meet our definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Because there is no identifiable healthy-group whole-brain task effect, exclusion criterion E5 applies (includes only between-group contrasts or lacks healthy-group task effect). Thus the study is excluded.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5. The task reported is a theory-of-mind (false belief, photo, false sign, true belief) vignette paradigm probing mentalizing/attribution of beliefs and attention, not goal-directed problem solving requiring planning, sequencing, or rule-based operations to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults: n=21, repeated-measures random-effects, whole-brain model/inference), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space; peaks in Table 1), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/peaks). Exclusion criteria met: none (does not report only ROI results, is not only group comparisons, includes within-group healthy task contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore excluded because I5 is not met.

The study investigates immediate implementation of verbally instructed stimulus-response and object-color mappings (instruction following, S-R/O-C mappings), not problem-solving as defined (goal-directed search/planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel solution). Although it reports whole-brain group BOLD results in MNI coordinates (tables) and thus meets neuroimaging reporting criteria, it does not involve critical thinking/planning or problem-solving processes required by I5. Therefore it does not meet the key content inclusion criterion.

Excluded because the reported voxelwise inference was restricted to a region-of-interest with small-volume correction (Analysis: "Inference restricted to: region of interest"), meaning the paper reports only ROI results (meets exclusion E3). The study does report BOLD data (I8), coordinates in MNI space (I7), and acceptable reporting (I9). However it does not provide a whole-brain group-level task effect with voxelwise inference across the whole brain (I6 not met). Additionally, the task is described as an executive/language Hayling Sentence Completion Test and is not clearly a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). Therefore the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task involves economic commitment/decision-making (accept/reject/defer prospects, bandit gamble) rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires planning/sequencing operations or applying rule-based computations to arrive at a correct solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults: multiple whole-brain, FWE cluster-level group analyses, n=20), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is economic decision-making, not defined problem-solving as required). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only restriction; whole-brain results are present). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study uses a reversal learning task (predicting reward/punishment for stimuli and updating responses after contingency changes), which is a reinforcement/associative learning/cognitive flexibility paradigm rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning, sequencing actions, and executing operations within a rule-based framework to arrive at a solution across domains). The paper does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD results (I8), and coordinate reporting is available in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore excluded because it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task).

The task is a moral judgment task involving evaluating dilemmas and making appropriateness judgments; it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The study does satisfy other methodological criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and provides voxelwise results in reported tables (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., results are not ROI-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore exclude because inclusion criterion I5 is not met.

This task involves verification of two-operation arithmetic problems combined with working memory retention, which fits the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations within a rule set). The study used task-based fMRI with BOLD measure, whole-brain model fitting (MNI coordinate space), and reports group-level voxelwise results (within-group and random-effects contrasts, corrected and uncorrected thresholds) with stereotactic peaks/tables. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the reported analyses are ROI-based (model fit over: region of interest; regions defined a priori in striatum) and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis is reported, violating I6 and triggering exclusion E3. The task is a reinforcement-learning/stimulus-action-reward association learning task, not a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met). The study does report BOLD measures and stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and coordinate reporting is acceptable. Inclusion criteria met: I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

The study uses a mental-rotation task in healthy adults (n=10) that requires a goal (judge stimulus parity) and mental transformations to reach the correct response, which fits the review's definition of a problem-solving task. It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses (GLM/ANCOVA) with inference over the whole brain; the coordinate space is MNI and reported peaks (3) are listed in a table; a BOLD measure is used. These satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain rather than ROI-only, the sample are healthy adults, and this is an empirical within-group task effect. Note: sample size is small (n=10), but this does not violate the stated inclusion/exclusion criteria.

The study uses a mental rotation task (Shepard–Metzler figures) which is a visuospatial transformation/same–different judgment rather than a multi-step problem-solving paradigm as defined by I5 (goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to reach a previously unknown solution). While the task requires mental transformation, it does not match the review's operational definition of problem solving. The manuscript does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level analyses are reported (I6), coordinate space is MNI with stereotactic peak tables (I7/I9), and the measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) data collected during tasks that include classic problem-solving/fluid-reasoning tasks (Matrix reasoning, Paper folding, Letter sets) that meet the review's problem-solving definition. Analyses were whole-brain (model fit over whole brain), group-level within-subject task effects are reported (simple effects with peak coordinates in tables), and coordinate space is MNI. The sample is healthy adults (n=174) screened to exclude dementia/MCI. The report includes voxelwise peak tables (reported peaks for each contrast). Therefore it satisfies I5 (problem-solving tasks), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only group comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical human data).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (analyses are region-of-interest only; model fit and inference are restricted to an ROI/SPM mask) and E5 (study includes only Parkinson's disease patients and reports no healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (coordinates reported in MNI space) and I9 (voxelwise peaks reported in a table). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not clearly meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task — contrasts labeled CRT/SUB suggest reaction-time measures, not problem solving), I6 (participants are patients with Parkinson's disease, not healthy adults), and I8 (measure is molecular tracer uptake—PET tracer uptake—not BOLD or rCBF). Given ROI-only inference and absence of healthy adult task-based whole-brain results, the study is not eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI BOLD whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults (n=9) reporting results in MNI space, so it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the task is a numerosity/magnitude comparison (compare number of dots vs color judgment), which is a perceptual/discrimination task and does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5) requiring goal-directed planning, sequencing, or executing rule-based operations to reach a solution. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task).

Exclusion decision rationale: This study does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The task is a Theory of Mind false-belief task (processing incongruent mental states), not a problem-solving task defined as goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the clear mismatch with the core review objective (I5), the study must be excluded.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. The task is an explicit action-planning task (goal cue vs. grip cue) requiring participants to plan/sequence object-directed actions to achieve a goal, which satisfies the problem-solving definition (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adults (n=16) (I6). Results are reported in stereotactic space (MNI) with peak coordinates (I7). The measure is BOLD functional response (I8). The NeuroStore record documents voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and reported peaks/tables, which satisfies acceptability of reported coordinates (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), the study is empirical and includes healthy-group task effects. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study must be excluded because it does not study a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5 not met). The task used is an Anti-Saccade Task (response inhibition/error processing), which does not meet the review's definition of problem solving (having a goal and requiring planning/sequencing critical-thinking operations to arrive at a solution). The paper does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults are reported), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise peaks reported in a table). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., results are whole-brain, include within-group healthy effects). fulltext_incomplete is false.

Excluded because the task (feedback-guided reversal learning) is a reinforcement/associative learning and decision-making paradigm rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no evidence of goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions or rule-based problem solving to arrive at a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (coordinate results reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the review definition).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the reported whole-brain contrasts are omnibus between-group tests and the paper does not report a healthy-group task effect (analyses are described as between-group/interaction contrasts and ROI group comparisons). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results in MNI coordinate space reported), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise peak coordinates reported in tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — task is conditioning/reinforcement, not a problem-solving task as defined; I6 — no clear whole-brain group-level task effect reported for healthy adults (only between-group omnibus contrasts). Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16) that investigates transitive inference/relational reasoning—a logical problem-solving task requiring integration of relations to reach a conclusion, which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The report includes whole-brain group-level GLM analyses (model fit over whole brain; group-level t tests) and BOLD measures (I6,I8). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and peaks/tables are provided (I7,I9). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not limited to ROIs, are within healthy-group task effects, and the paper is empirical.

The study used a mental arithmetic (algebraic) task requiring participants to compute and select correct solutions, which meets the review's problem-solving definition (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM analyses in healthy adults (n=22; ages 18–24) (I6). Results are reported in MNI space with tables of peak coordinates (I7, I9), and the neuroimaging measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). Multiple whole-brain within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., High Effort>Low Effort, Big Reward>Small Reward), so voxelwise task effects in healthy participants are available. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not only between-group or subgroup comparisons). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

Excluded because the reported analyses are ROI-based with no clear whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (Analysis 0 explicitly ROI; Analysis 1 lacks features indicating whole-brain analysis). This meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD measure reported), and I9 (peaks/coordinate results are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a perceptual/reward estimation decision task, not a problem-solving task as defined), and I6 (no evidence of at least one whole-brain group-level analysis). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the review and must be excluded.

This study does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task is decision-making under risk (affect-rich vs affect-poor choices/lotteries), not a problem-solving paradigm involving planning/sequencing actions to reach a goal or executing rule-based operations to derive a solution. The record does satisfy I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure), and I9 (coordinate tables reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I5).

This study is excluded because it does not examine task-based problem solving in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study does not include any healthy-group task effect; participants are methamphetamine-dependent patients and the paradigm is a resting-state scan). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results reported in MNI coordinate space), I8 (BOLD functional connectivity measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based problem solving paradigm; task is resting-state with eyes open), I6 (does not include healthy adult group-level task effects; participants are patients). Fulltext is complete for screening. Given these mismatches with the review objective (task-based problem solving in healthy adults), the paper must be excluded.

The study uses a mental rotation task (same/different judgments on rotated images of hands and tools), which is a visuospatial transformation task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to reach a solution). The record meets other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (I6), reported stereotactic coordinates in Talairach (I7), BOLD measure reported (I8), and coordinate tables provided (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore excluded because it does not meet I5.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (task is moral judgment of scenarios, not a problem-solving task as defined). It does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adults, n=29), I7 (reports coordinates in MNI space; reported peaks), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are met (E3–E6 not applicable). Therefore the paper is excluded for failing to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

The study reports an fMRI task (hierarchical rule task) involving goal-directed, rule-based selection from working memory consistent with problem-solving operations (planning/sequencing and rule-based execution) satisfying I5. It includes a whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analysis in healthy adults (n=22) with model fit and inference over the whole brain (I6). Coordinates are reported in MNI space with reported peaks (I7). The measure is BOLD response (I8). Coordinate results are available as reported peaks (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs (not E3), not only group comparisons of disease/age/gender (not E4), includes within-group task effects (not E5), and it is empirical human data (not E6). Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record. Overall, the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective of whole-brain task-based fMRI studies of problem solving in healthy adults.

The study uses a moral judgment (theory-of-mind) task rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined by the review. It therefore fails inclusion criterion I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). It does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Exclude because I5 is not satisfied; other inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study is an fMRI investigation of metaphor/conceptual expansion (creative cognition) using passive judgments of unusualness and appropriateness, not a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met). Analyses were conducted within predefined ROIs (model fit over region of interest; regions listed), and NeuroStore reports ROI-based results only, so it violates the whole-brain requirement (E3 applies) and thus fails I6. The study does report stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and BOLD measures (I7 and I8 met) and voxelwise results are reported in tables (I9 met). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because E3 is met and key inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met.

This study examines implicit false-belief (theory-of-mind) processing using Sally-Anne-style tasks and true/false judgments; it does not involve a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no goal-oriented planning, sequencing actions, or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is ToM/false-belief, not problem-solving). No exclusion criteria from the list apply (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text is complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study investigates moral evaluation/social cognition (justice sensitivity, praise/blame) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution). Although it contains whole-brain group-level BOLD analyses reported in MNI space (satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9), it does not meet I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper is excluded for failing to meet inclusion criterion I5.

This study does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). The task involved passive presentation of digits and number words with attention/foot-pedal checks and instruction to avoid movement; there is no goal-directed problem-solving, planning, or execution of rule-based operations to reach a solution. It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults; n=29), I7 (reports coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied (other inclusion criteria I6, I7, I8, I9 are satisfied; exclusion IDs met: none).

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5. It investigates Theory of Mind / pragmatic language (false-belief and coherent story comprehension), not goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to reach a solution. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). The paper uses a sentence-completion (Hayling) task and reports BOLD results in Talairach coordinates (I7, I8 met) with peaks in tables (I9 met). However, the task is not clearly a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met). Crucially, all reported analyses are between-group contrasts (controls vs. high-risk subgroups or patient subgroup comparisons) and no within-group, healthy adult task-related activation is reported; thus the study includes only between-group contrasts and does not provide a healthy-group task effect (violates inclusion I6 and meets exclusion E5). The reported results focus on disease-related group comparisons, satisfying exclusion E4 as well. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI BOLD data during explicit reasoning/problem-solving tasks (forced-choice problems with tourist cities and U.S. states), satisfying I5. Multiple second-level, group-level whole-brain analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; participants treated as random effects), satisfying I6. Coordinates are reported in ICBM152 stereotactic space (MNI-like), satisfying I7. The measure is BOLD (functional bold), satisfying I8. Voxelwise peaks and tables are reported (reported peaks, Tables t1–t3), satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (there are whole-brain contrasts), the sample is healthy adult participants (n=16), and the paper is empirical. Therefore the article meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5. It is an fMRI study of observing joint actions and shared intentions (social cognition), with tasks involving tracking intentions or colored dots, not goal-directed problem solving, planning, or rule-based solution operations. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). Excluded because it does not include any whole-brain, group-level task effects in healthy adults (E5). The study is a single-case (n=1) clinical patient (age 15) with a history of brain tumor and radiation-induced white-matter damage; the reported task is verb generation (not a problem-solving task). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach; reported peaks = 2), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise peaks/coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not qualify as a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adult individuals; sample is a single patient). The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults where participants silently read sentences and decide whether described volleyball actions are technically feasible — an evaluative decision task that entails critical thinking and evaluation consistent with the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (flexible factorial and conjunction analyses) with inference over the whole brain (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with reported peak tables (I7, I9), and uses BOLD fMRI measures (I8). There are task>rest and stimulus contrasts showing within-group task effects, so it is not limited to between-group contrasts or ROI-only results. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) appear to apply. Full text completeness: the NeuroStore record provided is sufficient for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although this fMRI study meets several methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults with BOLD measures reported in MNI space), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The task is a Stroop Color-Word conflict paradigm (response selection/attention/conflict resolution), not a goal-directed problem-solving task that requires evaluating the problem, planning/sequencing actions, or executing operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem solving task) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only reporting, not a patient-group comparison only, contains healthy-group task effects, and is empirical).

The Mental Clock Test requires participants to determine whether the angle between clock hands is <90° or >90°. This entails a clear goal and mental manipulation/operation applying a rule to arrive at a correct judgement, consistent with the review's definition of problem-solving (evaluating/planning/performing operations to reach a correct solution). The study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses (one-sample t-tests, n=20 healthy adults) with BOLD as the measure, uses Talairach stereotactic space, and provides coordinate tables. Voxelwise results and thresholds are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This study investigates intention understanding of observed gestures, not problem-solving as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, or rule-based solution operations). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses reported: Analyses 1 and 2 infer over whole brain), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported via tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task is action/ intention inference, not a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3–E6 not met). Therefore excluded for failing I5.

This study used a perceptual causality judgment task (participants judged whether one ball caused another to move) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task. Inclusion criterion I5 (task-based study of problem solving involving goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution) is not satisfied. The study does satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses reported), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space with peak coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (E3), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), includes within-group healthy task effects (so E5 not met), and is empirical (E6 not met).
